summary: Stores a registered API Console client's app data (Android package name, iOS bundle ID and App Store ID) used to build deep links.
Records where an embedded item was retrieved from by web fetch: input URL, retrieved URL after redirects, canonical URL, item types parsed (such as schema.org or Open Graph) and retrieval time.
why: Structured data fetch provenance including canonical and item types.

summary: Placeholder for transient generic data on an embed that is not saved on the server. It has no attributes.
A 128-bit identifier for an event such as a query, made from a process ID, server IP and microsecond timestamp.
Extra information returned by the ascorer to build snippets in GWS experiments: title and URL match info, query subitems and tidbits.
why: Snippet construction data including title and URL match.

summary: Records bitvectors of which query items match the title and the URL, and which items the snippet chooser considered.
why: Query matches against title and URL for snippets.

summary: Describes a query term, phrase or synonym used in snippet generation, with its text, weight, and flags for original, optional and highlighted.
Describes a snippet tidbit: its text with highlighted terms, position in the document, score, type, matched query items and anchor info.
Records on-domain and off-domain anchor counts for a tidbit that came from anchor text.
why: Anchor counts for anchor-based snippet text.

summary: Stores a packed representation of face data for an image in Mustang storage, with a version number.
Stores a compact Fatcat binary classification label for a document or site, with a discrete 0 to 127 fraction showing how much of a site the label applies to.
why: Document and site classification label in Fatcat.

summary: Stores the output of PetacatAnnotator for a page: Rephil clusters, up to 5 verticals per taxonomy (verticals4, geo, products_services, audiences), and binary page-type and sensitive-content results, plus a per-doc weight within the site (e.g. pagerank or navboost impressions).
why: Documented topical classification of documents, with site-relative weight.

summary: Holds the list of Rephil clusters assigned to a document inside the compact Fatcat classification.
why: Topic cluster container attached to a classified document.

summary: One Rephil cluster entry: a cluster id and a discrete weight from 0 to 127 that maps to 0.0-1.0.
Stores a document's classification against one taxonomy (by enum or by name), the classifier version, and the list of categories with weights.
One taxonomy category (id such as /Sports in verticals4) with a discrete weight from 0 to 127 representing 0.0-1.0; weights in a classification total 1.0.
why: Category weight in a document's topical classification.

summary: Stores a 16-bit weak hash of a contact detail (phone or email) and its type, used so the raw detail cannot be decoded.
why: Assistant/Focus contact data, not web search.

summary: Pointer that identifies a contact for the Assistant, using Focus contact ids, device raw contact ids, and secondary ids.
why: Assistant contact system, not web search.

summary: Identifies a device contact by its contact id and the device id it lives on, for Focus device contacts.
why: Assistant device contacts, not web search.

summary: Identifies a device by Android GServices id and a SHA256-based hash tied to the user and device, for device contacts.
why: Assistant device identity, not web search.

summary: Stores the raw contact id assigned on a device together with the device id.
why: Assistant device contacts, not web search.

summary: Holds additional device contact ids that are not actively used to match contact pointers to contacts.
why: Assistant contact matching, not web search.

summary: Stores a contact's secondary identifier: hashes of contact details, the full name, and a fingerprint of the name, used when the primary id does not match.
why: Assistant contact matching, not web search.

summary: Records attribution for a Knowledge Graph value: dataset, project, provider, statement, uri, and whether attribution must be displayed.
why: Knowledge Graph data attribution, no page signal.

summary: Holds the identifiers of a Knowledge Graph topic: the mid (machine id, the global primary key) and an optional id that may be a human-readable id.
why: Shared KG entity identifier type used by other structures.

summary: Represents a geopoint value (latitude and longitude in degrees) as one possible Knowledge Graph value type.
Represents a measurement value as a magnitude and a product of units, such as 5.2 meter^2 per second.
One unit in a measurement, with its power and the unit's Knowledge Graph id (a unit mid field is deprecated).
Holds a list of predicate and object pairs processed as a nested struct, which can be recursive.
Associates a Knowledge Graph property with its values for a topic, including total value count and a value status when no concrete values are present.
Represents a Knowledge Graph entity with its id and its property-value bindings.
why: Knowledge Graph entity record, referenced by other structures.

summary: Union-style Knowledge Graph value: bool, int, float, text, id reference, lat/long, measurement, nested struct or compound topic, with language, citation, provenance and timestamps.
why: Generic KG value container, no page signal itself.

summary: Core record for a crawled and indexed document: URL, DocId, content and original content, IP, crawl user agent, canonical equivalence class, and flags for the NoIndex, NoFollow, NoSnippet, NoArchive and related robots reasons. It also stores PagerankNS (the production PageRank value) and a deprecated Pagerank field.
why: Documented document record with PagerankNS and robots restriction reasons.

summary: Main content section of a document record: crawled body representation, content type, encoding, language, crawl time, content length and geometry annotations.
why: Crawled content and crawl time stored for indexed docs.

summary: Holds snippet and title metadata (category, description, title, language, URL) made available to snippet code, originally from the Google Web Directory and other sources.
why: Title and description metadata feeding snippets.

summary: Stores the original unconverted document (typically PDF or Word) before conversion, without HTTP headers, with its uncompressed length if compressed.
why: Original non-HTML document content kept for indexing.

summary: Generic snippet response returned for a result: snippet HTML lines, title HTML (possibly truncated, with query-term markup), per-doc debug info, an experimental ranking snippet field, and snippet-specific response data.
why: Snippet and title output shown for search results.

summary: Records actions supported by Madden for a local entity: guest checkout, asynchronous restaurant reservation, and the reservation flow URL.
why: Assistant reservation actions, not web search.

summary: Describes an access point linking a feature to another feature (for example an airport that gives access to a city), with feature id, type, points on or off a segment, position along the segment and unsuitable travel modes.
Represents one parsed field of an address, such as street or locality, with its feature link, parsed names, optional range, text affixes and type.
Stores the unparsed lines of an address in display order, with the language of those lines.
Represents an address, partial address or address range attached to a Geostore feature, with unparsed lines, parsed components, template id and field metadata.
Represents a range of numbers within an address component, with numbers, interpolation parameters, prefix, suffix and same-parity flag; used for segment address definitions and references.
Stores the id used to fetch a feature's geometry from the 3D Geometry Store.
Container for a speed limit value tagged with a trust level.
Holds structured client-specified data attached to a Geostore feature, identified by attachment id and client namespace, with type id, comment and the message payload.
Represents the unique id of a Geostore attribute, with id, provider id and type.
Attaches an attribute and a typed value (boolean, numeric, string, enum, proto) to a Geostore feature, with display names and field metadata.
Stores a language-specific display name (synonym) for an attribute value.
Lists the materials found on a physical barrier lane marker.
Records the best-match locale feature for a feature and the localization policy used to select its local name.
Stores the id of a BizBuilder listing, used to query the BizBuilder backend; indicates a feature is claimed.
Represents a line of division between two features of the same type (such as two countries), with the left and right area features, legal status, status overrides and logical borders.
Describes a physical lane marker that bounds a lane or lane connection, with adjacency fractions along the flowline and marker, and which side it sits on.
Holds building-specific attributes for TYPE_COMPOUND_BUILDING features: base height, floors, height, levels, default display level and structure.
Holds data specific to business chain features, namely canonical GConcepts describing the ideal categories of the chain's members.
Stores a weekly schedule of opening hours for a business together with Geo-specific field metadata.
Holds a business-owner call to action: its type and a URL.
Represents a canonical GConcept (category) of a business chain's members and whether it must be present on a member.
Stores an S2 cell covering for a feature as a list of S2 cell ids.
Custom proto representation of part of the CityJSON spec: city objects, flattened local vertices, a transform to ECEF coordinates and appearance materials.
Holds predefined materials that geometric primitives in a CityJSON proto can reference.
Describes a single material for a geometry surface: diffuse color, smoothness, name, shininess and transparency.
Stores an RGB color with each channel in the range 0 to 1.
Represents an object with geometry in a CityJSON proto, with an id, type (such as building) and its geometries.
Represents geometry of a city object at a given level of detail as points, surfaces or solids, with semantics.
References a predefined material by index from a geometric primitive.
Represents a single line, loop or set of points as indices into the flattened vertex list.
Represents a collection of standalone surfaces with no prescribed topological relationship.
Stores the semantic type of a geometric primitive, used to reason about surfaces.
Represents a 3D shape as a watertight exterior shell with optional interior shells.
Represents a polygonal surface as a closed exterior loop with optional interior loops, plus material and semantics references.
Defines how to convert vertices from a local coordinate system to a new one using a scale and a translation.
Stores the x, y and z offsets used in a coordinate transform.
Generic item proto for business listings, with optional call to action, job metadata, media, names in several languages, offered status, price, price format and a ranking hint for item ordering.
Stores a count tagged with a comparison operator, for example axle or trailer count.
Describes the pattern, border line and colors of a crossing stripe such as a crosswalk, stop line or yield line.
Holds curvature values at points along a flowline, linearly interpolated between points.
Describes a curve connecting two externally specified endpoints, either Bezier or circular.
Holds the internal Bezier control points for a curve connection (one for quadratic, two for cubic).
Defines a Bezier control point by an angle and a distance multiplier relative to the straight edge between curve endpoints.
Stores the arc radius for a circular curve connection.
Describes a data source used to build the Geostore repository: provider, copyright owner and year, description, release info, attribution URLs, raw metadata keys and importer build details.
Represents a date and time as seconds since the Unix epoch with a precision value.
Stores a dimension (height, width or length) with unit, tagged with a comparison operator.
Stores a numerical dimension value with its unit.
Holds data used to render a POI on a map, currently the display location.
Stores information about disputed areas: which power administers it and which countries claim it.
Holds the type for TYPE_DOODLE features.
Records a cost that applies based on duration of use, with free flag, periodicity, price per currency and a start and end range in seconds.
Represents raster digital elevation model data with blend order, data levels, child data availability flags and the elevation tile data.
Holds elevation data for a feature: average elevation in meters and peak details for peaks and volcanoes.
Holds attributes for TYPE_ENTRANCE features: allowance and whether the target can be entered or exited through it.
Models a relationship between a feature and one of its entrances or exits by feature id.
Holds establishment-specific attributes for business features: BizBuilder reference, regular and exceptional opening hours, price info, service area, telephone numbers and a deprecated type.
Stores exceptional (non-regular) hours for a business such as holiday hours, with the date range and the weekly schedule applied.
Records a feature's existence state: closed flag and reason, start and end dates, removed flag and reason, and a deprecated birth timestamp.
Holds provenance information for sub-fields of a feature as a list of field-path and provenance pairs.
Pairs a set of feature field paths with the provenance that applies to them.
Records feature history timestamps in the Geo repository: birth, last modification and removal, in microseconds.
Records feature id forwardings: which feature this one duplicates (directly or transitively), which features duplicate it, and forwarded and replacement ids.
A simple list of feature ids with no duplicates.
A 128-bit globally unique feature identifier made of an S2 cell id and a 64-bit fingerprint; immutable once assigned.
Holds general metadata about a Geo repository feature: bulk-update flag, version tokens, replacement info, field metadata, id forwardings and history.
Represents a feature property as an abstract id, keyed by field type with extra ids for attachments, attributes or Knowledge Graph properties.

The top-level Geostore record: a typed feature with id, names, addresses, geometry, establishment data, hours, website, a 0.0-1.0 rank field with rankDetails, relations, status, source info and many type-specific extensions.
Tracks feature derivations and replacements: features this one was derived from and features that replaced it.
Internal field-level metadata available to upstream providers but not to read-only consumers; wraps internal metadata.
Tracks rights for a feature property id, recording the minimum rights level among its current values.
Wrapper that holds data about a lane's track, plus reserved curvature.
Describes one option of a menu item (such as chicken, beef or tofu): names, price, calories, nutrition facts, ingredients, allergens, portion size, preparation, spiciness and photos.
Denotes an ingredient of a food dish, with names in multiple languages.
Denotes the serving portion size of a dish as a quantity and a unit.
Represents a menu item with names in several languages and a list of options that carry prices.
Holds a GConcept id (a category in the Geo Ontology), its prominence for the feature, and field metadata.
Defines a feature's geometry as the union of included features' polygons minus excluded features' polygons.
Holds a Geometry Store id and, in some contexts, the footprint and geometry materialized from that record.
Stores unsimplified water-subtracted polygons for a feature as seen by the rest of the world and by the administering country.
Stores geopolitical overrides for a feature: attribution conveyed to a region, region-specific names, and regional polygon adjustments and composing claims.
Holds raw polygons to add to or subtract from a feature's base polygon to build a region's view.
Holds the recipe for a region's view of a feature's geometry: disputed-area claims included or excluded for that region.
Records the relative altitude (grade level) of a segment at an indexed point, such as freeway versus overpass.
Represents HTML text associated with a feature, such as descriptions in several languages, with a type.
Defines a feature's geometry as the union or exclusion of other features' geometry, with links in both directions between composite and composing features.
Holds internal data about other data in a feature: polygon shape ids, per-field rights status and trust signals.
Internal field metadata recording whether data was generated automatically and a summary of the source providing it.
Internal-only segment info for editing clients: disallowed lane connections, disallowed primary connections and positive travel allowances.
Specifies a single outgoing lane connection between a lane on this segment and a lane on another segment.
Records the data provider and dataset (or algorithm name) from which a piece of Geostore data was generated.
Models a real-world (logical) intersection by grouping topological intersection features, with parent and child groups and a group type.
Holds attributes for TYPE_INTERSECTION features: segments that terminate there, its intersection group and toll cluster.
Holds metadata for a job (service) item of a business: duration, related categories, job type id and the matching Knowledge Graph mid.
Stores a category (gcid, language, name) that a user picked a job type from at input time, used to group jobs.
Stores the Knowledge Graph mid that a Geostore feature refers to.
Associates a road segment with a landmark feature, with feature type and the travel modes for which the landmark is useful.
Holds attributes of physical lane markers: barrier materials, crossing patterns and linear stripe patterns.
Describes an individual road lane for schematic rendering and navigation: markers, flow line, connections, restrictions, width, surface, number and type.
Records how a road lane connects to a lane on another road segment in Geostore, including the bounding markers, flow line, lane number and whether it is the primary continuation.
why: Maps road-lane data, unrelated to web search.

summary: Stores a piece of text together with its language code in Geostore (Maps data).
Documents a logical building level (floor) feature in Geostore, storing the buildings it belongs to and its elevation number relative to ground level.
Stores a linear road marker made of one or more parallel physical lines, ordered left to right, in Geostore.
Records details of one language within a Geostore locale: whether it is official, a preference value, and the speaking and writing population percentages.
why: Maps locale data, not web search.

summary: Describes a locale meta-feature in Geostore: the geographic extent of localization preferences, the languages spoken there and a localization policy ID.
Groups border features that together model a divide between two regions in Geostore, with the border segments and a legal status for the group.
Stores a media item (photo URL, media key, format, size) attached to an element of a Geostore price list.
why: Maps price-list media, not web documents.

summary: Stores the original width and height in pixels of a photo attached to a Geostore media item.
Stores a name for a Geostore feature (street, place, building, etc.) with language, full and short text, flags and field-level metadata. It can also hold opaque IDs such as postal codes.
why: Maps feature naming, not web search.

summary: Container holding all GConcept (category/ontology concept) instances associated with a Geostore feature.
Holds the public GConcept instance plus private fields (inferred or edit-added flags, provider, source dataset) for a Geostore feature's category concept.
Represents opening hours for a Geostore feature: a regular weekly schedule plus date-delimited exceptions.
why: Maps hours data, not web-search ranking.

summary: Stores operational information for a Geostore feature, namely records of temporary closures such as remodels or vacations.
Records a country-specific override of a border's display status in Geostore, for example hiding a border on one country's maps domain.
Stores the logical color category (e.g. yellow) of a painted road element in Geostore.
Describes parking allowances for a Geostore feature: allowed vehicle and service types, permits, discounts and time-based rates.
Describes parking facilities provided by or available to a Geostore feature, including allowances, opening hours, availability and restrictions.
Expresses when and for which vehicle or service types parking on a road is prohibited in Geostore.
Stores topographic prominence in meters for peak and volcano features in Geostore.
Models a pedestrian crossing in Geostore: angle, width, offset, type, restrictions and whether crossing anywhere is allowed.
Describes a single physical road marker line in Geostore: paint color, pattern, dash and gap lengths and materials.
Stores road curvature in radians per meter along a line, with the fraction of the line where it starts to apply, in Geostore.
Stores a latitude/longitude point (scaled by 1e7) with optional field metadata in Geostore; widely referenced by other geo structures.
Stores a Geostore point plus its altitude in meters relative to ground level.
Stores political-region data for Geostore features: capital, claimed features, GDP, literacy percent and population.
Stores a sequence of vertices connected by geodesics, with field metadata, as a polyline in Geostore.
Stores a spherical polygon in Geostore, mostly in encoded S2 form, with optional height, base and an unsuitable-for-display flag.
Stores an object's position and orientation (lat, lng, altitude, yaw, pitch, roll) in Geostore.
Records nutrition facts (calories, fat, carbohydrate, protein, sodium, cholesterol) for a food dish in a Geostore menu.
Stores a calorie range with lower bound, upper bound and unit for a food dish.
Stores a nutrient amount as a lower and upper bound with a mass unit for a food dish.
Stores price list information (such as food menus), the URLs that provide them and a verified-status record for a Geostore establishment.
Records whether a provider-supplied price list is verified; the docs say only verified listings should be displayed.
Stores names, descriptions, language and IDs for price lists, sections and menu items in Geostore.
Represents a price list such as a food menu for a Geostore establishment, with names, sections, cuisines, availability times and source URL.
Stores one section of a price list (such as a menu section) with its items, media, call to action and names in Geostore.
Stores a price range for an attribute in Geostore: currency, lower and upper price and units.
Records what is known about a feature property when no specific value is present, for now mainly that the feature is known to have no value.
Stores the dataset and provider that referenced Geostore data came from; a minimal version of source info.
Embedded in a Geostore feature, records rank-calculation details: the available rank signals and the signal mixer used to compute the final rank (Oyster Rank).
why: Maps feature rank, not web-document rank.

summary: Represents one rank signal for a Geostore feature: a 0-1 Oyster Rank estimate plus the raw scalar or string behind it and a signal type.
why: Maps feature rank signal, not web search.

summary: Stores an arbitrary key-value pair of source data from a provider, attachable to a Geostore feature's source info.
Documents a raw-data key in Geostore: its label, description and how conflicting values are merged.
Stores a latitude-longitude rectangle as two opposite corner points in Geostore.
Stores a feature name per region and language in Geostore, for example differing names for a body of water in different countries.
Stores restrictions that apply to a polygonal area in Geostore, which may limit routability of segments inside it.
Records a geographic or logical relationship from one Geostore feature to another, with the other feature's ID, type and metadata.
Groups road restrictions that share the same underlying cause across a region in Geostore, listing the segments that refer back to the group.
Documents a road restriction in Geostore: a set of conditions (schedule, travel mode, vehicle attributes, subpath) under which an action such as a turn cannot be taken.
Records rights information for a Geostore feature as a list of fields that carry rights.
Defines conditions (time schedule, vehicle types and attributes) that determine when road traversal information applies in Geostore.
Models a traffic-monitoring device (speed or red-light camera) and the road segments it may observe, so navigation can warn users.
Describes one component of a road sign in Geostore: its row and column position, type, text and the feature it points to.
Holds the details of a road sign in Geostore as a list of its components and their relative positions.
Stores metadata about the association between a road segment and a route in Geostore, such as display preference and route direction.
Documents a route feature in Geostore, a logical group of segments such as a named road or highway, and records the feature type of its children.
Holds a type attribute for school district features in Geostore.
Describes an ordered path through a short set of road segments in Geostore; currently used to list segments a road sign applies to.
Large Geostore structure describing a road segment: speed limits, lanes, restrictions, routes, grade, surface, toll status, crossings, landmarks and geometry sweeps.
Stores ramp-specific properties for a road segment in Geostore, namely the highest priority of connected road endpoints.
Represents the geographic area served by a Geostore establishment as a list of served features, with constraints applied by editing middleware.
why: Maps service-area data, not web documents.

summary: Defines an ordered reference to a transit station or platform served by a line variant in Geostore.
Holds a type attribute for ski boundary features in Geostore.
Holds a type attribute for ski lift features in Geostore.
Holds difficulty and type attributes for ski trail features in Geostore.
Stores a road slope value (elevation change over horizontal distance) and the fraction along the segment where it starts to apply.
Stores virtual GAIA IDs assigned to a Geostore feature, including the robot GAIA ID used when a business has been claimed.
The canonical Geostore record of data provenance: provider, dataset, release, collection date, attribution URLs, raw data and the user behind the data.
Records a trust level for the input source (feed or user) of an observation to help Geostore feature summarization; a higher enum value means a more trusted source.
why: Maps source trust for geo features.

summary: Documents a speed limit in Geostore: its category, source type, the conditions where it applies and a constant, unlimited or variable value.
Stores a speed value and unit; values are kilometers per hour in Geostore.
Represents a way to traverse nested Geostore fields by referencing their version tokens, starting from an externally specified root message.
Selects one field by number, and optionally a repeated entry by its version token, as one step in a Geostore stable field path.
Stores the 2D polygon connecting two road segments at an intersection, used for rendering real road width in Geostore.
Stores a telephone number and related details for a Geostore feature: contact category, shared-number flag, type, callable locations and metadata.
why: Maps business phone data, not web documents.

summary: Stores temporary closure information for a Geostore feature as the latest possible start and end dates of the closure.
Represents text with a language that is prepended and/or appended to a primary text in Geostore.
Stores a triangular 3D mesh in indexed form: a points array with height and triangle vertex indices.
Defines a parking-style rate that applies based on utilization times, with start and end time restrictions, duration-based rates and a tax-included flag.
Stores a time component as the intersection of a list of time intervals, with a component type, in Geostore time schedules.
Encodes a point in time at varying granularity (second up to year) for Geostore intervals; missing larger fields mean the interval repeats.
Encodes a time interval or named occasion in Geostore, with begin and end endpoints and an option to represent the complement of the range.
Encodes a schedule as the union of time components; referenced by many Geostore structures such as hours and restrictions.
Stores the time zone identifier related to a Geostore feature, with field-level metadata.
Stores the toll intersection features that make up a toll cluster, a collection of points where traffic pays a toll, in Geostore.
Describes sequential travel across one or more toll clusters in Geostore, which may entail paying a fee or toll pass.
Stores a toll cluster feature and its position along a toll path in Geostore.
Holds the set of toll clusters in a toll path with their positions; ordering relies on each cluster's index.
Stores an indexed track as a list of poses (position and orientation) along it in Geostore.
Documents a transit line in Geostore: the agencies operating it, label colors, stations it can go through and the vehicle type.
Stores a specific variant of a transit line in Geostore: a reference to its line concept and the ordered stops it services.
Encapsulates information about an individual transit station in Geostore, namely the agencies that service it.
Records the association between a transit station and an agency servicing it, including the station code within the agency's network.
Wraps trust signals for the source of a Geostore observation, typically based on historical evidence or status such as an internal operator.
why: Maps source trust for geo data.

summary: Marks a speed limit without a limit value, used to indicate the absence of a speed limit in Geostore; it has no attributes.
Holds a list of URLs in Geostore, usually translations of a single URL.
Stores a web location for a Geostore feature with language and field metadata, and a deprecated pagerank field (valid values 0 to 65535).
why: Maps feature website; pagerank field deprecated.

summary: Identifies a human user of Geo data, such as an editor, with an encrypted Gaia ID, key name and optional username, to describe data sources.
Marks a dynamic speed limit that can change with road, traffic and weather conditions in Geostore; it has no attributes.
Defines a set of vehicle attribute conditions (weight, height, length, width, axles, trailers, hazardous goods) used to select a slice of vehicles in Geostore.
Stores the relative vertical ordering level of a Geostore feature among overlapping features, such as freeway versus overpass.
Stores a weight value tagged with a comparison operator, used in Geostore vehicle filters.
Stores a weight as a numeric value and unit in Geostore.
Gives an element in an OCRed Goodoc document a reference address (anchor) that logical-entity links can point to.
why: OCR document structure, not web search.

summary: Stores a pixel bounding box (top, left, width, height, optional label) for page structure elements such as pictures, paragraphs and characters in OCRed documents.
Specifies a simple partition of a bounding box into a sequence of sub-boxes, for example coarse symbol boundaries within a word, to save space.
Records a break label type on an OCR element and whether the break comes before the element.
Records per-character OCR details: font, size, color, bold/italic/underline flags, recognition confidence, suspicious flag and a garbage-detector penalty.
Top-level representation of an OCRed document in Goodoc: header, pages, logical entities, sub-documents and editing history.
why: OCR document structure, not web search.

summary: Holds the OCR engine ID and version and the font table for a Goodoc document.
Maps a font ID to a font name in a Goodoc document header.
Describes one OCRed page: size, DPI, blocks, text confidence, garbage-detector info, a porn-classifier score for images on the page and page-level stats.
Describes a block on an OCRed page: type, bounding boxes, orientation and reading order, paragraphs and text confidence.
Records the OCR engine ID and version of a source Goodoc whose text was merged into a page, such as a PDF text layer.
Stores aggregated statistics for one font size over a range of symbols: median character and line measurements and counts of lines and symbols.
Aggregates optional characteristics of OCR page elements: anchor, break, character, language and semantic labels.
Stores a BCP47 language tag with a weight for how likely the language is to appear in input text.
Records a detected language for an OCR element with a closest language ID, a 0-100 confidence and a language code set by the garbage text detector.
Represents a logical entity in an OCRed document as a group of links into the Goodoc, with metadata; specific kinds extend it elsewhere.
Stores a link from a logical entity to a Goodoc element, by anchor or by document, page, block, paragraph, word and symbol indices, or by URL.
Encodes one ordinal component of a printed or inferred page number: numbering style, value, delta and an optional section component such as a chapter.
Groups orientation details for an OCR element: deskew angle, mirrored flag, orientation, text line order and writing direction.
Specifies structure overrides that force certain Goodoc-to-HTML renderings, such as treating a page as an image, skipping it or replacing a word's HTML.
Holds a CSS attribute name and value to apply as an extra style override when rendering Goodoc content.
Represents a paragraph in OCRed content: bounding boxes, indents, spacing, alignment, dropped cap, routes, orientation and text confidence.
Stores the bounding box and letter count of a paragraph's dropped capital letter in OCRed content.
Describes a text route within an OCR paragraph: start and end points, a weight and the words along the route.
Stores a rotated pixel bounding box with an angle, able to represent non-axis-aligned page elements in OCRed documents.
Stores a route index and word index (both starting at 0) marking a point on a text route in an OCRed Goodoc paragraph.

Labels a logical part of OCRed page content (mostly blocks or paragraphs): alternate text, attributes, chapter start, page continuation flags, flow, page number, column, table, content-link and snippet-filter details.
why: OCR/Books content labeling, not web search.

summary: Records the column number and total column count for an OCR element labeled as a column.
Records that an OCR-labeled span links to other content: a URL target, a scholarly citation target or an in-volume target.
why: OCR link label, not web links.

summary: Stores citation details for a scholarly-citation label in OCRed content: authors, title, year, bibliography key and a confidence value.
Stores an in-volume link target and confidence for caption, footnote pointer, table-of-contents, index or continuation labels in OCRed content.

Stores the camera location from IPTC (city, state, country, sub-location, world region); deprecated in favor of location_created.
Stores a location (city, state, country, sub-location, world region) for where an image was taken or what it shows.
Documents the EXIF and IPTC metadata extracted from an image: camera and lens, exposure settings, GPS position and heading, author, copyright, description, title, keywords and software.
why: Records embedded image metadata, including GPS and copyright.

summary: Stores an inspiration score from 0 to 1 used in the featured image search project, describing how product-related or inspirational an image is.
why: Single score for a niche image feature.

summary: Documents the crawl state of an image: result code, not-crawled reason, whether the state is terminal, robots-blocked agents, dedupe cluster repid, noindex timestamp and URL deletion.
why: Image crawl and indexing state, including robots handling.

summary: Stores a web relevance score computed during image selection, describing how relevant an image link is to the web page it is on.
why: Page-to-image relevance score from image selection.

summary: Organizes shopping offer information from the Inventory and Policy Service: an offer ID and inferred image types.
Stores basic per-document image data: filename, width, height, flags and a deprecated entropy and color value.
Stores a debug string for the overall image porn classifier.
Stores click signals for measuring image quality: clicks and good clicks defined using GVE.
why: Click counts used for image quality measurement.

summary: Stores the IDs of up to five people entities and media entities with the highest topicality in a document, used by the Skin Tone Twiddler to check if a result set is dominated by one entity.
why: Document-level entity topicality annotation used in a twiddler.

summary: Documents one region in an image: bounding box and score, labels, product flag, visual-neighbor score and Starburst features.
Stores an image with its detected regions plus image-level scores (porn, violence, pedo, racy), indexing flags and precomputed restricts.
why: Image region container with safety scores.

summary: Stores speech recognition signals generated for a video in Amarna: raw Cloud Speech results, language ID input, recognizer metadata and a stitched transcript.
Undocumented. Holds a sequence of frame-level feature data (inferred from field names: frame signals for video understanding).
Stores a blob ID and update timestamp for Amarna's frame-level signals blob.
why: Blob pointer for video pipeline signals.

summary: Stores the status and reason why Amarna could not provide per-document information for an image.
Stores extra per-document data for animated images: aggregated SafeSearch porn scores and total duration in milliseconds.
Stores metadata for a requested video transcode: itag, Venom genus and ID, state, expiration and xtags.
Stores a case-sensitive name and value pair (an xtag) that distinguishes a variant of a transcode.
Stores a collection of xtags with unique names associated with one piece of content.

Documents information derived from fetched video bytes in Amarna: media info, duration, transcripts and speech data, language ID, thumbnails and previews, frame-level embeddings, SafeSearch and porn scores, video anchors, Venom status and unwanted-content flags.
why: Large video index record covering video previews and transcripts.

summary: Stores crawl-status debugging information: a status code and the reason an item was not crawled.
why: Records why an image or video was not crawled.

summary: Stores a Deep Image Engagingness score for an image.
why: Single image-level score, scope unclear from docs.

summary: Documents whether a stored file is complete, truncated or unknown relative to the original online, with a lower bound on the original size.
why: Storage completeness flag for media files.

summary: Identifies a frame of a video by timestamp in milliseconds and by variant: multi-thumbnail, preview frame zero or thumbnail.
Marks a frame as one of the multiple thumbnails generated per minute of video; the message has no fields.
why: Empty marker type for video frames.

summary: Marks a frame as the first frame of a video's generated preview, with preview length and the xtags used.
Marks a frame as a thumbnail of the video; the message has no fields.
why: Empty marker type for video frames.

summary: Stores frame-level Starburst V5 embeddings of a video at 1 frame per second, or a blob ID pointing to them.
Stores the per-document image data (ImageData) for one video frame, identified by frame identifier, or the error that prevented generating it.
Stores a list of per-document image records extracted from video frames.
Records decisions on whether an image was generated by Google's tools, based on watermark logits and a fingerprint nearest-neighbor score.
why: Detects Google-generated images only, per the docs.

summary: Stores the language identification input used for an ASR transcript: S3 top locale, YouTube captions audio language and whether the locale was stripped.
Stores a NIMA image score.
why: Single image-level score, scope unclear from docs.

summary: Stores debugging details for S3 language identification of audio: input cap, segment counts and duration, stride and wave header.
why: Debug info for video speech language ID.

summary: Stores S3 language identification results for an audio chunk: whether it contains speech, start and end time, the language result, model version and frame counts.
Stores trimmed metadata about the S3 speech recognizer used: mode, model info label and service name.
Stores one frame's embedding with its time offset in the video.
Stores the list of all frame-level embeddings of a video.
Stores product recognition information for an image from VSS: up to two versions of product sets with embeddings and localization scores.
Stores a normalized bounding box (x, y, width, height from 0 to 1) for a recognized product in an image.
Stores a recognized entity ID with a normalized recognition score between 0 and 1.
Documents one recognized product in an image: category IDs, detection score, embedding, entities, feature type, bounding box and retrieval token groups.
why: Product recognition detail for shoppable images.

summary: Stores a model name and its integer tokens used for retrieval of a recognized product.
why: Retrieval token detail for product recognition.

summary: Stores the products found for one version of the VSS models, with model type and version number.
Stores one alternative transcript hypothesis from speech recognition, with confidence and word-level information.
Stores a speech recognition result for a portion of audio: ranked alternatives, channel tag, language code and result end time; copied from the Cloud Speech API format.
Indicates that an image or video is to be deleted from the repository for legal reasons or hidden from search results, with deletion and hide reasons.
why: Flags media to be removed or hidden from search results.

summary: Stores one Venom status per genus a video belongs to, for example found on the web or opted in by an Interest Feed partner.
Documents a video's status in the Venom pipeline: genus, state, ACL, settings, insertion and deletion timestamps, attempt counts, transition and Venom ID.
Stores a list of video links that were not indexed.
why: Records video links on pages that were not indexed.

summary: Stores a video URL with crawl-status debugging information explaining why it was not indexed.
why: Per-URL crawl status for video links not indexed.

summary: Stores debugging info for video previews: last Amarna processing time and processing engine.
Stores a generated video preview: the bytes, debugging info, preview metadata and the preview's first frame.
Documents properties of a video in Amarna: URL, crawl state, first and last crawl and processing timestamps, audio-only flag, content-based metadata and which verticals index it.
why: Video crawl and index record with crawl timestamps.

summary: Records which verticals a video is indexed into; a video can be in verticals without being in video search.
Stores per-word speech recognition information: the word, start and end time, confidence and speaker tag.
Stores lists of reasons why YouTube videos were filtered from specific processing, such as previews.
Stores SafeSearch scores for an image from Google Brain: porn, racy, violence, medical, spoof, child-related and Images Universal inappropriateness, plus a version string.
why: Image safety classifier scores, not a web page signal.

summary: Stores SafeSearch OCR annotation for text in an image: prominence score, porn score, and offensive and vulgar scores weighted by prominence.
Stores a list of matches for offensive symbols detected in an image, as part of image SafeSearch content classification.
why: Image SafeSearch symbol detection, not web document signal.

summary: Records one offensive-symbol match in an image: the symbol type and a confidence score (higher means more likely to match the symbol).

Stores, per page, which image links were selected for image search indexing and which images lack data yet (selected or rejected), with their crawl status. Used by consumers of docjoins that need the full list of image URLs on a page.
why: Image selection and indexing status for images on web pages.

summary: Documents license data for licensable images: license URL and type, copyright notice, creator, credit text, the page explaining how to acquire a license, and where each value was sourced. Also carries SafeSearch flags.
why: Image license metadata extracted from web pages.

summary: Pairs an image URL with its image link selection info, recording how that image was considered for image search selection.
why: Wrapper pairing image URL with selection info.

summary: Records an image URL on a page that has no image data yet, with the reason (Amarna status) and crawl-status debugging details.
why: Debug data for images not yet indexed.

summary: Packs image recognition output for one detected bounding box: feature embeddings, label groups, and the box region. Leave the region unset for a whole-image annotation.
why: Image-understanding container, no documented web ranking signal.

summary: Holds a list of image-understanding annotations, one per bounding box detection.
Stores an image feature embedding in several formats (raw bytes, floats, int values, tokens) plus a version and local-feature image template.
Records a detected image region: a normalized bounding box, the box confidence score (how likely it contains an object), and a version.
Stores one image label with human-readable text, a Knowledge Graph entity id, confidence score and metadata (for topicality, visible labels, attributes).
why: Image labels tied to KG entities, image-side only.

summary: Groups the labels produced by one model (or models sharing a version), such as classifier, visible-label or noun-plus-attribute results.
Stores a named metadata value (float or string) attached to an image label or feature.
why: Generic metadata helper for image annotations.

summary: Stores bad SSL certificate information for a canonical URL so it can be included in docjoins and pushed to serving time. Records the URL the bad certificate came from when it differs from the source URL (a redirect target).
why: Per-URL bad SSL certificate data passed to serving.

summary: Records an alternate localized URL for a document: language/region, where the annotation came from (e.g. a sitemap feed), device match info and URL encoding. Relates to hreflang-style alternates.
why: Localized alternate URLs and their annotation source.

summary: Stores raw redirect information for a document: the final redirect target found from rendering or the crawler, the redirect chain from rendering, and how many rendering hops were kept.
why: Redirect targets and chains recorded at indexing.

summary: Holds the chain of redirect hops from the current hop's target to the final target. Present for redirecting URLs and absent for the final target.
why: Redirect chain structure for crawled URLs.

summary: Records one hop in a redirect chain: the target URL, the target with fragment, and the redirect parameters.

Records characteristics of a detected server or content redirect: type, delay in seconds, whether it came from rendering or the crawler (meta redirect), whether it is a download, and whether the frame target denies framing.
why: Redirect type and timing details stored at indexing.

summary: Documents three versions of a document's content: the original crawled content, the processed content indexed in Web search, and an intermediate version no longer generated. Stored as ordered ranges.
why: Original versus processed indexed content storage.

summary: Stores one ordered range of content marked as original-only, processed-only, intermediate or shared, with size, source type (e.g. frame or iframe), source URL and optionally compressed text. Used to rebuild each content version.
why: Range storage behind original and processed content.

summary: Collects robots information for a document from sources such as HTTP headers and meta robots tags: noindex, nofollow, noarchive, nosnippet, noimageindex, notranslate and similar reasons, max snippet length, max image preview, and an unavailable_after content expiry.
why: Robots directives and snippet/preview limits per document.

summary: Stores shingle fingerprints (possibly larger than 64 bits) with metadata describing how the fingerprint was computed.
why: Fingerprint utility type used for duplicate detection.

summary: Holds the primary identifier of a production document (the document key, equal to the Alexandria row key representing a URL and its crawl context), plus experiment ids for double indexing and index-dups experiments.
why: Document identifier plumbing with experiment ids.

summary: Records signals that identify a spike of spammy anchor phrases: spam phrase count, days to discover 80% of them, rate, fraction of anchors, demoted and processed counts, spike start and end, and a combined penalty. Anchors created during the spike are tagged as phrase spike.
why: Anchor phrase spam spike signals tied to link anchors.

summary: Summarizes output of the anchor spam penalizer: counts of spam phrases, demoted anchors and demotion period, trusted-source matching, a predicted spam probability and a combined spam penalty. Spammy anchors are demoted to SPAM locality.
why: Anchor spam probability and penalty stored per document.

summary: Documents anchor statistics for a docjoin: anchor counts by locality (on-site, on-domain, off-domain, local, forwarded), dropped and redundant anchors, spam log-odds, anchor spam info, and Penguin fields (last update, page-level penalty from 0 good to 1 bad, early anchor protection, too many sources).
why: Anchor counts, spam and Penguin penalty fields per document.

summary: Records anchor counts per duplicate-forwarded URL: anchors kept, off-domain, redundant and scanned counts, collection type, the dup URL and the last scan time.
why: Per-duplicate anchor counts feeding anchor statistics.

summary: Records how many redundant anchors were dropped per (domain, text) pair when a domain sends many anchors (all but 200 are thrown out). Capped at 10,000 entries.
Records how many anchors were dropped for a domain because it exceeded the per-domain phrase cap.
why: Documents per-domain anchor phrase cap drops.

summary: Summarizes anchors from one trusted site used in anchor spam checks: site name, tokenized anchor text, trusted score (fraction of pages with newsy anchors), spam-phrase count and a KL-divergence match score against spam anchors.
why: Trusted-source anchor data used in spam classification.

summary: Holds extra information, apart from annotations and the raw cdoc, used for building the final composite document.

Tracks the version and update timestamp of each piece of data (signals, annotations) attached to a CompositeDoc. About 537 fields, each naming one data item, so it doubles as a catalog of signals and annotations stored per document, including navboost, NSR, site authority, anchors, dates and spam items.
why: Catalog of per-document data names; versions only, no values.

summary: Stores the version info for one piece of data on a document: a human-readable version, the timestamp of the last update (or deletion), and a consideration timestamp noting an attempted update when no data exists.

Records a serving-time cluster id for pages that represent the same content but are not identical (translated or paginated pages). Only one member of a cluster is shown to the user; also stores the reason and member index.
why: Serving-time clustering of near-same pages like paginated or translated.

summary: Holds the set of serving-time cluster ids used to de-duplicate results at serving; a document can be in different clusters for different properties.
why: Set of clusters used to dedupe at serving.

summary: Records one locale entry of a computed localized alternate: the alternate URL, language/region code, region extracted from the URL (TLD or path pattern), cluster id and device match info.

Stores localized-variation clustering for a document: the clusters it belongs to, hreflang, in-body and outlink target link sets, detected document language, source-blocker flag for boosting, and Sitedup rule ids and warnings.
why: Localized cluster data including hreflang link sets.

summary: Records one localized cluster: id, type, language and region represented by the URL, whether filtering applies (keep one result per cluster on a SERP), and debug info.
why: Localized cluster record with SERP filtering flag.

summary: Old-format cluster info (no longer populated for documents processed since July 2014) holding a fingerprint of outlinks, link members of the cluster and unvalidated outlinks.
Records an unvalidated outlink in the old link-based cluster info: URL, annotation source and crawl timestamp.
Records a verified member of an old link-based cluster: URL, language codes and annotation source.
Describes a localized URL that a document links to in a localized-variation context: link data, metadata, target document data and a validation status.
Records basic info about a localized link target: the URL, whether the link is cross-domain, and where and with what language annotation it was found.
why: Localized link target with cross-domain flag.

summary: Records where a localized link was discovered and its language code: the language code from hreflang or outlink, anchor text for outlinks, annotation source and the sitemap feed URL if from a sitemap.
why: Source of hreflang-style language annotations including sitemaps.

summary: Records when a localized link was first seen (defaults to last crawl) and when it was last verified against the linked document's data.
Holds direct target links (A links to B) and indirect target links (A links to B which links to C) used in localized clustering.
why: Direct and indirect localized link sets.

summary: Stores data about a URL being validated in localized clustering: detected content language, crawl status and timestamp, whether it is canonical, and its outgoing hreflang link data.
why: Target page data used to validate hreflang clusters.

summary: Carries rendering output for a document into the docjoins: the DOM and render tree, converted contents, embedded resources and their fetch info, rendered snapshot image with quality score, redirect info and rendering metadata.
why: Rendering output and embedded resources attached to documents.

summary: Records all external resources needed to render a page (CSS, images, scripts, iframes): the embedder info, per-resource link info, page size info, summed HTTP response length and uncrawled link URLs.
why: Embedded resources needed to render the page.

summary: Stores an importance value for a page as an embedder, with the link info for the embedding page.
Logs how many URLs on a host finally went to the crawler (trawler) during rendering, with named counters.
Stores a named counter with a count, used inside per-host rendering fetch counts.

Collects metadata annotated by the fetch server for an embedded resource: crawl status, whether it is an ads, critical or trivial resource, smartphone user-agent fetch flag, number of crawler fetches, rewrite method and robots info.
why: Fetch metadata for resources loaded during rendering.

summary: Records one embedded link: URL, content type, size before and after decompression, full HTTP response length, crawl status, timestamp and duration, cacheability, fetch status and source, and robots-denied flag.
why: Per-resource fetch details for page rendering.

summary: Records the Unix timestamp of when each rendering output field (document data, rendered snapshot) was last generated, to control how often costly fields are regenerated.
Records page download size information: number of resources and images, how many have content crawl status, and summed HTTP response length of the embedder and all referenced resources.
why: Page resource counts and download size.

summary: Tracks rendering cache use: when rendered content expires, last render time, the cache used, and simhash distances for crawled and rendered content.
Holds a single rendering request config parameter, virtualTime. No description is given for it.
Stores a host-to-count mapping of how many embedded links on each host went to the crawler during rendering.

Stores small values from rendering output in the Alexandria document table: render exceptions, render time, importance, percentage and number of new tokens found after rendering, render engine and cache stats, snapshot and render tree quality scores, and whether resources were missing.
why: Rendering results including new tokens found after JS render.

summary: Records that a URL should be in the rendering corpus: the render effort and which selector made the decision.
Stores one vertical classification for a document: id, name, Petacat id and a probability between 0 and 1.
why: Vertical classification of documents with probabilities.

summary: Records the desktop interstitials signal for a document: details of detected interstitials, an overall policy-violation flag, pipeline epoch and pattern, and a URL tree of interstitial patterns for the host as a site-level signal.
why: Documented interstitial policy-violation signal for pages.

summary: Optional details of the interstitial signal computation: basic interstitial info and whether the value is smeared (extrapolated from other URLs).
Stores basic info for one detected interstitial: its geometry in absolute page pixels, content type, detection mode and layout type.
Carries Core Web Vitals field data (CLS, FID, INP, LCP) in the VOLT signal, extracted from UKM aggregated 75th-percentile data.
why: Core Web Vitals field data attached to documents.

summary: Stores the VOLT per-document data used for ranking changes: mobile and desktop Core Web Vitals plus flags for whether the display URL is HTTPS. Mobile friendliness is stored separately; safe browsing and BAS/AER conditions are not used for ranking.
why: Per-document CWV and HTTPS data noted as used for ranking changes.

summary: Stores a list of restriction categories describing access requirements for a document.
Stores state data for an adaptive frequency estimator, with interval and prior-weight values for clicks (good and total), CTR-weighted impressions, dwells and LocalUniversal dwells.
why: Estimator state for click and dwell frequency per URL.

summary: Accumulates decayed (half-life weighted) coverage data for a URL: impressions, chances, clicks (good, bad, image, total, unclassified), CTR-weighted impressions, dwells, last impression/click/dwell dates, and first-seen and first-coverage timestamps.
why: Documented per-URL click, impression and dwell aggregates.

summary: Stores an aggregated numeric signal across matching URLs (used by NumericSignalAggregator): mean, deviation, percentiles, min and max URL, sample URLs, counts of matched URLs and URLs with signal, and running variance state.
why: Aggregation of per-URL scores across URL patterns.

summary: Stores the internal state (mean, m2, total weight) of the West and Chan running mean and variance algorithm, accessed through a utility class.
Holds click signal data for a URL pattern and its parent pattern, as SccSignal messages.
Records click counts for a URL pattern: total, bad and image clicks, the number of URLs and image URLs, plus debug fields.
Contains the signals needed for per-URL click prediction, used by Index Selection for scoring: coverage data, pagerank score, pattern and regexp pattern scores, SCC data and prior signals.
why: Per-URL click prediction inputs including pagerank, used in index selection.

summary: Container for any prior signal used in scoring, pairing a prior signal id with an aggregated score, so URL pattern signals can extend beyond pattern and pagerank scores.
why: Extensible prior signal container for URL scoring.

summary: Represents the numeric signal of one URL: score, weight, the URL, first-served timestamp, whether it carries an important signal, and weekly performance record count.

Documents properties of spoken content based purely on the media file: audio duration (and estimate with confidence), speech duration, word count, recognizer accuracy, spoken language, audio-only flag and truncation flag.
why: Speech properties of audio and video media files.

summary: Represents a dominating branch of a URL tree, kept separately so documents on smaller branches are not dropped during sampling. Stores URL features, a pattern id and a payload.
Records one URL feature (type, value, fingerprint and grouping) used to split URLs into patterns.
why: URL feature used in pattern trees.

summary: Holds a list of URL features.
Stores a URL tree for a site: nodes (root first), big branches, a key or site, build and retrieval timestamps and extra info. Used to group URLs of a site into patterns.
why: Site URL pattern tree used to attach signals to URL groups.

summary: Stores debug info for a URL tree: an inner similarity value.
Defines the unique id of a URL tree through crawler id, domain and hostname.
Records one node of a URL tree: parent, child subtree indexes, the splitting URL feature and its information-gain score, pattern id for leaves, path from root and payload.
Captures output of analyses on automatic speech recognition transcripts: how many ASR segments were classified, how many were gibberish, and the gibberish result.
Stores per-document Kaltix rank values: KaltixRank (about 2 bytes for the top 1B), plus LocalKaltixRank and SiteKaltixRank, noted as empty for now.
why: Per-document rank value, two fields noted as empty.

summary: Wraps a list of region codes with the type of region signal to use in data governance.

Configures the 'any value' type, which accepts any non-empty value for a slot in Google's intent/meaning schema (Knowledge Answers, used for query understanding). It carries only shared contract and remodeling metadata fields.
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Configures the attribute type (a value that must be a schema attribute, optionally limited to a list of attribute ids) for a slot in Google's intent/meaning schema (Knowledge Answers, used for query understanding). It carries only shared contract and remodeling metadata fields.
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Configures the yes/no value type for a slot in Google's intent/meaning schema (Knowledge Answers, used for query understanding). It carries only shared contract and remodeling metadata fields.
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Configures the collection type (value must be one of listed /collection/* ids) for a slot in Google's intent/meaning schema (Knowledge Answers, used for query understanding). It carries only shared contract and remodeling metadata fields.
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Configures the compound type (a value composed of multiple answer values) for a slot in Google's intent/meaning schema (Knowledge Answers, used for query understanding). It carries only shared contract and remodeling metadata fields.
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Undocumented. Holds a list of slot names (inferred from field names).
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Configures a date value type in the intent schema, with flags for which date resolutions are allowed (day, month, year, hour, symbolic time, holidays, and so on). Used when parsing dates in queries for Assistant-style intents.
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Undocumented. Groups container, intersect, same and union type configs for dynamic typing (inferred from field names).
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Records how a piece of data in a query was resolved from elsewhere in the query or a previous query, such as a pronoun resolved to an earlier entity.

Configures the duration type, with an optional min/max range in milliseconds for a slot in Google's intent/meaning schema (Knowledge Answers, used for query understanding). It carries only shared contract and remodeling metadata fields.
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Configures an entity value type in the intent schema, limited by KG collections, KG ids or identifiers, with optional geolocation exposure. Used for query parsing.
why: Assistant intent-schema type config, no web-document signal

summary: Describes how a facet is read from neural or lexical parse output, naming its facet, input slot and output slot.
why: Query-parsing structure, not a web-document signal

summary: Stores grammar and syntax signals attached to a parsed query intent: language, alternate language, definiteness, mood, plurality, tense, polar-question flag and sentiment.
why: Query-intent parsing metadata, no web-document signal

summary: Bundles signals from the annotation layer of Google's unified intent generation (TUIG), one slot per annotator type such as Qref, Nimble, NTPR and semantic annotators.
why: Query-intent annotation plumbing, no web-document signal

summary: Holds a list of path components that identifies one argument inside a nested intent function call.
One step in an argument path: an argument name plus a zero-based index that tells apart same-named sibling arguments.
Represents one argument of a parsed intent function call: its name, schema slot key, value, modifiers, signals and token-span evaluation data.
Records where an intent argument's value came from: the current query, a previous query, an anaphor, an attentional entity, a prior task state, a search answer value or injected schema.
Marks an argument value carried over from an attentional entity published by a dialog, with a key to recover it and mention properties.
why: Assistant dialog context, not web search

summary: Marks an argument value that comes from the current query, storing the query span(s) and an optional neural location annotator marker.
Marks values carried from contextual schemas injected by biasing configs for particular clients. It has no attributes.
Marker message used to say which annotator annotated an argument in the current or previous query. It has no attributes.
Marks an argument value carried over from a previous query or a QRef-annotated entity, storing spans, the previous event id, role and source.
Records the intent id and slot name that a carried-over value played in the previous query.
Undocumented marker with no attributes. Name suggests a value derived from a previous response's meaning (inferred from name).
Marks an argument value derived from a previous dialog task state, storing the dialog intent state id, intent name, argument path and list or function-call carry-over details.
why: Assistant dialog state, not web search

summary: Marks a value carried over from a presented candidate in a dialog (such as picking 'John A.' from a list), storing the candidate index.
Marker for a value carried over from the previous function call in a dialog. It has no attributes.
Records that the current query contains an anaphor (such as 'it') that refers to an earlier value, with the spans where it was annotated.
Marks an argument value carried over from a search answer value shown for an earlier query, storing event id, value index, metadata index and display text.

Large bag of per-argument signals for a parsed query intent: entity grounding and QRef confidence, collection membership, provenance, location data, personal-entity scores, shopping ids, support-transfer data and annotator flags.

Holds the value of an intent argument as one of many typed forms: nested function call, date/time, number, money, location, person, media, calendar event, shopping types and other Assistant custom types.
Stores an attribute id and its completion score for an entity-attribute intent.
Records which KG collection an entity argument belongs to, with the collection id, mid, score and typed scores.
why: Query-intent entity annotation, no web-document signal

summary: Undocumented. Holds a score type and score value for a collection (inferred from field names).
Holds a concept id: meaning captured in a continuous space instead of the MRF schema, attached to an intent expression.
Stores the Concepts data epoch id used to annotate queries.
Represents a value that points to another part of the same meaning tree, using an argument path from the root.
Stores extra data needed at the intent-fulfilment phase for custom vehicle action arguments, as a free-form map.
Marker for annotations from the freetext annotator. It has no attributes; its presence is enough for conformance checks.
Represents one parsed intent as a function call: name, arguments, marker, modifiers, sensitivity, ignored and unexplained query tokens, concept info and signals.

Stores function-call-level signals for a parsed query intent: confidence level, grounding and parsing signals, prefulfillment ranker inputs and scores, close-interpretation flags, local and shopping signals and dedup records.
why: Query-intent ranking plumbing, not web-document signals

summary: Records how well a parsed intent was grounded: counts of groundable, grounded and constrained arguments and a groundability score used by the prefulfillment ranker.
References a specific entity of a given type (such as a timer id) by id string and id type.
Stores signals for QRef implied entities merged into an entity argument during parsing: mid, annotated span, QRef confidence and shopping ids.

Documents a prototype Mustang/Kgraph attachment that encodes intent-language (IQL) expressions annotated by Webref and Pianno, such as page-level intents, as compressed bytes with Pianno confidence scores. Noted as not yet output in production.
why: Index attachment encoding page-level intents; prototype, not shown live

summary: Stores signals for one Local result in an intent query: geo intents from its gcids and a salient term set.
why: Local-result intent dedup for answers, not web ranking

summary: Holds per-Local-result signals plus a minimum salient-term similarity, used by the Packer to dedupe and check Local categorical derived intents.
why: Answers-packer intent dedup, not web ranking

summary: Records the type of lightweight token (such as FROM or TO) that extended an argument's span in a parsed query.
Stores the name of a media entity and, for songs, the primary artist, as signals on an intent argument.
why: Assistant media intent, not web search

summary: Stores signals from Munin function-call annotations: soft modifier collections, whether a modifier is isolated, and whether argument text was generated instead of taken from the query.
Marker for annotations from the NTPR annotator. It has no attributes; presence is enough for conformance checks.
