A cuisine constraint (such as Chinese or Thai) for a local query, stored as a GCID.
Undocumented. Holds an EV charging connector type constraint (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Holds an EV charging payment network constraint (inferred from field names).
An EV charging speed constraint for a local query, ANDed with other EV constraints.
A distance or extent in a query, with numeric value, units and a flag for non-specific values like 'a few'.
A GCID (business category ID) filter constraint, populated in Superroot.
A health insurance network constraint for provider searches.
Flags for accommodation sub-types (hotel, resort, hostel, vacation rental, ryokan and others) used by the hotels team to classify query intent.
Info on hyper-reliable local categories: a flag, commodity strength, retrieval GCIDs and GCID score overrides.
Holds GCIDs and scores for hyper-reliable categories, set only when hyper-reliable is true.
Flags for implicit local intents in a query, such as gas station, gym, bank, hotel or post office.
The joiner text and type between two locations in a query, with its byte span.
Holds IDs a local assistant needs to look up a result: Geostore feature ID, address, KG mid, position and rect.
A location in a query: basic, compound or vicinity, with constraints, text, byte span and any resolved local result.
A set of constraints on a location in a query, such as amenities, cuisine, price, quality, chain, hours, menu item and EV charging, combined with AND.
One element of a location in a query, typed as an alias, business name or category, directional modifier, QRef, SAFT or personal reference location.
A menu item used as a location constraint or standalone element, stored by menu item ID such as 'thai curry'.
A price constraint with cheap, moderate and expensive flags, min and max price, and currency code.
A quality constraint such as best, highly rated or star ratings for local queries.
A constraint on minimum bedrooms and bathrooms for a hotel or vacation rental.
A scalable attribute intent (such as outdoor seating or happy hour) used as a location constraint or standalone element, stored by attribute ID.
Undocumented. Holds a service type constraint (inferred from field names).
Star rating constraints, mostly for hotels, as OR-combined flags from one to five stars with half steps, plus or-more and or-fewer.
An area around a base location defined by an extent and a connector, such as '50 miles from here'.
A constraint on whether a location has been visited before.
The contact type (mobile, home, work) in a communication query, with original and normalized text.
A communication recipient in a query: contact, business name, email, phone number, relationship or calendar event, with raw text and annotation sources.
Stores a relationship contact in a spoken query: the alias used (e.g. 'mom'), its canonical form (e.g. 'Mother'), and a lexical entity ID for it. Used in Assistant-style query parsing.
why: Assistant query-parsing type, not web search.

summary: Records the device a spoken action should run on, as an optional device type (phone, tablet, watch) and an optional device name. Part of semantic parsing of voice queries.
why: Voice-assistant device argument, not web documents.

summary: Stores the name of a device (e.g. Nexus 5) as raw text, plus evaluation data meant only for internal Aqua use.
Encodes what a user refers to in a dialog turn: list selections, ordinal indexes, and mentions of the overall task. Used by dialog-referent grammar rules in query parsing.
why: Dialog understanding for assistant, not web ranking.

summary: Records a user's selection from a list of alternatives, by item ID, offset (ordinal such as 'first one') or matched raw text.
Annotation for an album named in a media voice query (e.g. 'The White Album'), with flags such as favorite, first, latest and play-more.
why: Media voice-query annotation, not web search.

summary: Represents a music recording requested in a voice query, where each filled field (artist, album, genre, movie, podcast, radio, etc.) adds a constraint on which audio is meant.
Metadata for an audiobook: the audiobook and book entity MIDs, authors and narrators.
Annotation for a book named in a media voice query (e.g. 'East of Eden'), with raw text, a 'latest' flag, and a QRef link.
Annotation for a cast device (Chromecast, TV, Chirp) in a media query, covering personal devices, common device names and device-type-only mentions, with device ID, name and quantification.
Stores a localized price as a currency code and a price value, used in media offers.

Documents a provider deeplink for media and its restrictions: allowed or blocked countries, platforms, subscription offers, paid offers, validity window, tags and a document score used to rank action links.
Stores a start and end timestamp (seconds since epoch) during which a media deeplink is valid.
Holds free-form text describing a media item (e.g. 'the episode with all of the comedians').
Encodes a constraint on a podcast or show episode in a voice query: absolute or relative index, release date, and a description.
Stores a terrestrial radio frequency as a band (AM/FM) and a value in MHz or KHz.
Annotation for a video game named in a media query (e.g. soundtrack requests), with raw text and a QRef link.
Annotation for generic music requests such as 'my library' or 'some music', with a new-music flag and raw text.
Stores a latitude and longitude pair in degrees.
why: Generic lat/lng used for radio station location.

summary: Annotation for a media entity: name, artist, content type, images, provider deeplinks, and type-specific info for news, podcast, radio, YouTube playlist, purchase and rental.
Wraps a list of MediaAnnotation entries so media annotators can annotate a span without an explosion of interpretations.
Describes a media provider (name, MID, KG key, media ID) and the deeplinks it offers for a media item.
Annotation for a movie named in a media voice query (e.g. 'Casablanca'), with raw text, provider metadata and a QRef link.
Annotation for a music artist named in a voice query (e.g. 'The Beatles'), with favorite and play-more flags.
Annotation for a music genre in a voice query (e.g. 'British Invasion'), with raw text and a play-more flag.
Annotation for a playlist named in a voice query (e.g. 'gym playlist'), including a flag for long-tail mood-based playlists and a normalized name.
Metadata for a news audio/video result: doc ID from the News360 backend, content type, publication time and publisher.
Annotation for a news topic in a voice query (e.g. 'ukraine' in 'read me news about Ukraine').
Records BUY and RENT offers for a media item with their localized costs.
Annotation for a podcast named in a voice query (e.g. 'This American Life'), with raw and normalized text.
Metadata for a podcast: cluster ID, episode GUID, RSS feed URL, title, and recommendation features used to train reranking models.
Stores a video provider's deeplink URL (e.g. a Netflix title link) and the provider MID.
Records order type and purchase timestamp for a purchased media item.
Encodes how many devices a query refers to, as a lexical word (e.g. ALL) and/or a number (e.g. 'three speakers').
Annotation for a radio station in a voice query (e.g. '107.7 the bone'), with partial frequency, favorite flag and raw text.
Metadata for a radio station: frequency, location, and a popularity value between 0 and 5 used in ranking stations.
Annotation for a radio network in a voice query (e.g. 'npr', 'bbc').
Records rental timing for a media item: purchase time, grant period, activation period and ownership end time.
Encodes a season constraint in a voice query (e.g. 'season 2'), as absolute or relative index.
Annotation for a song named in a voice query (e.g. 'Hey Jude'), with favorite, first, latest flags and a QRef link.
Annotation for a TV show named in a voice query (e.g. 'Breaking Bad'), with provider metadata and a QRef link.
Stores YouTube-specific deeplink info: a click-tracking ID and the uploader channel ID used to build a channel page URL.
Records counts for a YouTube playlist: total videos and videos playable in WoodStock.
Stores a currency as a Knowledge Graph MID.
Represents a money quantity as a number amount plus a currency.
Corresponds to an entry in a hand-curated table of news providers, carrying provider annotation data and raw text.
Describes the device or devices on which an action should be performed, usable as an action argument.
Annotation for a person named in a query: name, normalized text, alternative names, and whether it is a personal contact, with contact data and a personal-reference annotation.
Encodes a recurrence rule for repeating tasks: frequency, every-N multiplier, start, end, and daily, weekly, monthly or yearly patterns.
why: Reminder recurrence parsing, not web search.

summary: Records when in the day a repeating task should trigger, as either a time of day or a day period.
Encodes a monthly recurrence: absolute or from-end-of-month days, or the nth weekday of the month.
Encodes how a recurrence ends: an end date-time, an absolute timestamp, or a number of occurrences, with auto-renew fields set by the server.
Encodes when a recurrence begins, as a date-time or a timestamp in milliseconds.
Encodes a weekly recurrence as a set of weekdays plus start and end fields.
Encodes a yearly recurrence as a monthly pattern plus a set of months of the year.
Stores a brand mentioned in a shopping query as raw text and/or a Knowledge Graph MID.
Describes a merchant in a shopping query: name, KG MID, and Merchant Center IDs (including local and GSX identifiers).
Records a Merchant Center ID with flags showing whether it is used for GSX, local or PLA purposes.
why: Merchant Center ID wrapper for assistant.

summary: Represents a product offered by a merchant: shopping offer doc ID, merchant, price, product, and optional physical store.
Holds one phrase parsed from a shopping query, which can be a brand, offer, product or unrecognized span.
Describes a purchasable product: catalog ID, KG MID, catalog title, min and max price, and media-product attributes.
Stores confidence scores (0 to 1) that a product phrase names a book, movie or video game, plus a video-game flag.
Represents an expression in a user query describing one or more products: ordered phrases, grammatical gender and number, classification and shopping list item info.
Describes a purchasable media product with author, genre, title, order in series and topic attributes.
Stores a media attribute (such as an author) as a Knowledge Graph MID and raw text.
Stores a product mentioned in a shopping query as raw text plus catalog or media product metadata.
Records the item ID and list ID of a shopping list item tied to a product expression.
Describes a merchant's physical store: local store ID, name and location.
Marks a span of a shopping query that could not be identified as any other phrase type, storing its raw text.
Encodes a fraction in a query: numerator, denominator, optional whole number, and decimal precision.
Encodes a number found in a query: raw text, normalized value, simple or fraction form, spelled-out flag and a modifier such as 'more' or 'less'.
Encodes a simple number with its normalized value plus the decimal mark, digit grouping delimiter and system seen before normalization.
Wire-equivalent clone of a personal-intelligence entity: raw name, QRef annotation, and airline config when the entity is an airline.
Holds a personal reference in a query (e.g. 'my hotel') and its resolutions to personal entities, for personalized intents.
Represents a slot in an Actions on Google parse: entity ID, parameter name, matched original text, byte span, and a value, list or map of values.
why: Actions on Google slot, not web search.

summary: Represents a date, time or date-time from an Actions on Google parse, with a date, time of day, time zone and a property describing it.
Records whether a matched date-time is a date, time or both, and how it relates to the request's reference date-time.
Wraps a list of slots so a list can be used as a possible slot value.
Wraps a map of named slots so a structured value can be used as a possible slot value.
Holds one or more possible values for an Actions on Google slot.
Represents one actual slot value: a date-time, a string, or an on-device typed value.
Holds a typed slot value (boolean, date-time, number or string) returned by on-device Heron.
Annotates spans of a query with entity IDs (Freebase/KG mids) and collection information, plus confidence scores, cluster membership, related entities, locations and personal-data provenance.
why: Query-side entity annotation, not a documented page signal.

summary: Records a collection ID (e.g. /collection/us_states) an annotated entity belongs to, with a score slated for deprecation.
Records a relationship between two annotated entities: which implies the other, and the names of the relationship links.
Stores a Merlot category ID and confidence for an annotated entity, derived from collection membership.
Tracks each individual cluster an entity belongs to, with cluster ID, set score and sibling MIDs.
Stores a relation between an annotated entity and another entity MID, such as generalization, equivalence or support transfer, for downstream use.
Identifies a pronoun or nominal mention in a query resolved to an entity, with raw text and the referent's name.
Identifies a measure in a query such as '53 pounds': its category, raw text and numeric value.
Marks a sub-span of query text with one semantic annotation: a coreference, entity, measure or title span. Exactly one field is set per annotation.
Defines a category (syntactic like NNS or semantic like $Mass) for a sub-span of the raw query text.
Represents a single byte of a UTF-8 text sequence with a pointer to the document that contains it.
why: Generic NLP data-schema type, no signal.

summary: Represents one Unicode character with pointers to its containing document, paragraph, sentence and token.
why: Generic NLP data-schema type, no signal.

summary: Represents a single document in the NLX data schema: ID, URL, text, languages, authors and pointer spans over its bytes, characters, tokens, sentences, paragraphs and mentions.
why: Generic NLP schema; carries no documented ranking signal.

summary: Represents an entity that may occur several times in text: free-form name, machine ID (e.g. Freebase MID), type labels and gender.
why: Generic NLP schema entity, no signal.

summary: Records a span of text written in one or more languages (BCP-47 codes), with byte and character ranges.
Records a mention of an entity in a document: mention text, kind, type (named, nominal, pronominal), tokens and the entity it refers to.
why: Generic NLP schema mention, no signal.

summary: Represents one paragraph with its text and pointers to its document, sentences, tokens, bytes and characters.

Standard NLX data schema container holding lists of bytes, characters, documents, entities, language spans, mentions, paragraphs, sentences and tokens, plus presence metadata for each layer and field. Presence usage is noted as ad hoc.
why: Generic NLP schema container, no signal.

summary: Represents one sentence or utterance with its text and pointers to its document, paragraph, tokens, bytes and characters.
Represents a word or punctuation token with part-of-speech tag, dependency head and label, and pointers to containing sentence, paragraph and document.
Deprecated record of one dependency-parse edge for a token: relation label and head pointer.
Records metadata for an article item in a Woodwing file: author, category, description and title.
Holds Ocean (Google Books) data returned in docserver results for whole documents, as a doc tag.
why: Google Books doc info, not web search.

summary: Stores Google Books (Ocean) document data returned with search results: titles, authors, cover and thumbnail info, page numbers, pagerank of a book page, pricing, viewability, source and content types, and book, magazine, newspaper, patent and catalog specifics.
why: Google Books snippet metadata, not web search.

summary: Stores book-specific fields in Google Books results: auxiliary bibkeys, imprint, publisher, publication date, edition number, subject and numbering ranges.
Copies volume or part numbering ranges (e.g. 'Volume 1', 'Parts A-D') used to render numbering in Google Books results.
Stores catalog-specific fields in Google Books: whether it is the latest issue, publication date and display text such as 'Spring 2002'.
Records a contributor name and the highest-ranking contribution type for a Google Books volume.
Stores magazine-specific Google Books fields: display date, issue description, issue and numbering ranges, items in the issue, serial title and volume.
Stores newspaper-specific Google Books fields such as newspaper name, publication date and article roll coordinates; several are marked Atlantis-specific and deprecated.
Stores patent-specific Google Books fields: application, issue and publication numbers and dates, assignee, classifications, language and thumbnail path.
Records the work cluster a Google Books volume belongs to: work ID and cluster size.
Stores a price for Google eBooks as an amount in micros plus a currency code.
Holds Google eBooks sale prices per locale.
Stores a Google eBooks offer price for one country, plus the time the book goes on sale if not yet sellable.
Stores an image's height and width in pixels, used for Google Books covers.
Documents how a Google Books volume may be viewed in one locale: view type and reason, percent of the book shown, ads, download, copy and print rights, effective dates and the imprint source.
Stores the date a locale's viewability takes effect, allowing future books to be pre-indexed.
Records how a locale's viewability was derived, including the publisher imprint that provided the rights.
Stores per-document data in the Ocean (Google Books) index: volume ID, page ID, page number, page count and flags such as rights and availability.
Records commercial access rights a partner grants for a Google Books volume: copyable and printable percent, download limits, text-to-speech, public domain treatment and display limits.
Records access rights computed from partner and book metadata: family sharing, internal-only viewability and internal-only panelization.
Holds display attributes for a Google Books volume, currently the Creative Commons license type.
Stores commercial information for a Google Books volume from its imprint: buy-the-book text and URL, logo, promotional text, rights flags, percent shown, title and author strings.
Holds a Google Books volume's default viewability plus per-locale viewability entries, and whether the indexer updated it.
Pairs a two-letter country code with the viewability that applies to a Google Books volume in that locale.
Stores a bounding box around a line, word or symbol of OCR text: top-left position, width, height, rotation angle and an optional curved box.
why: OCR geometry for photos, not web documents.

summary: Stores a sequence of points approximating a curve for curved OCR text boxes, duplicated to allow on-device builds.
Stores one x and y point on a curve used in OCR bounding boxes.
Describes a curved text box by a mid-line curve, thickness and a top-to-bottom direction flag.
Stores recognized text with its bounding box, text block ID, content type and optional per-symbol widths.
Documents the key for official-pages data: a specially normalized query plus country and language. The docs stress it is not a raw query.
why: Key type for official-pages data, carries no signal itself.

summary: Holds a set of official-pages keys (normalized queries with country and language) and matching query-country-language fingerprints.
Stores a document ID with its entities encoded as entity candidates. Little else is described. Sits in an entity-per-document structure.
why: Entities attached to a document ID.

summary: Undocumented. Holds a value and a confidence value, apparently for PairwiseQ scoring (inferred from field names).
why: PairwiseQ score and confidence pair, no description.

summary: Stores versioned PairwiseQ scores used for experimentation: a version ID, a PairwiseQ value and its confidence value. Copied from the quality_nsr_pairwiseq package.
why: Versioned PairwiseQ quality score tied to NSR code.

summary: Records, per application (e.g. Gmail), a list of context-specific states describing whether something is treated as internal or external.
why: Workspace/People internal-external state, not web search.

summary: Stores a context type and a state value for the internal/external evaluation of an application.

Per-document record shared by indexing and serving that holds a large set of page-level fields: spam scores (gibberish, keyword stuffing, SpamBrain), original content score, NSR site data, dates (semantic date, last significant update), PageRank variants, onsite prominence, language, geo, and YMYL classifier scores. It points to many sub-messages and is decoded during the search phase.
why: Core per-page store of documented spam, quality, date, link and topicality fields.

summary: Free-form debug event attached to per-document data, with a source tag, message, value and timestamp.
why: Debug logging record, carries no documented signal.

summary: Identifier pairing an alias type with a sub-id for a saved personal alias (such as home or work) in a Maps personalization system.
why: Maps personalization alias, not web search.

summary: Stores a subset of a user's saved place alias (feature id, name, address, lat/lng, sticker) used for alias resolution in Search and icons in Maps.
why: Personal Maps alias data, not web documents.

summary: Metadata about a user's local discovery preference setting, such as dietary or cuisine, including the UI entry point and recipe context.
why: User personalization settings, not web document data.

summary: Records the recipe document id and URL from which a user's local discovery preference setting came.
why: User preference context, not a web ranking structure.

summary: Undocumented. Holds a Phil data string (about 70 bytes for the top 500M pages) and a version number inside per-document data; purpose beyond that is not described.
why: Undocumented per-doc blob; nothing on its meaning.

summary: Stores animation properties for a photo or movie: duration, loop count and number of frames.
Flags that an image contains Dynamic Depth metadata and which version (v1 or v2) it uses.
Holds the four core image metadata fields (caption, copyright, creator, credit) for one metadata segment such as EXIF, XMP or IPTC.
Stores GDepth XMP block details for a depth map: near and far distance, format, mime type, units and source dimensions.
Describes whether and how an image carries HDR information, pointing to gainmap details.
Flags which gainmap-based HDR formats an image supports: Adobe HDR, Apple HDR and Google UltraHDR.
Large catalogue of EXIF, IPTC and XMP image metadata fields (camera, lens, GPS, dates, captions, copyright, panorama, motion photo) extracted from an image. Almost every attribute has no description.
Flags whether an image is a spherical panorama or a VR180 image.
Stores a bounding box (min and max x and y) relative to image width and height.
Holds a list of single-precision floats used as a feature vector in object recognition.
Records the geolocation of a point or group of points for an image: latitude, longitude, altitude, country code, GPS flag and error bounds.
Stores a global image feature (such as DELG) as a tagged, versioned feature vector, optionally quantized.
why: Vision feature data, not web document signal.

summary: Holds local and global features generated from one image, plus image id, URL, dimensions, geolocation, region of interest and object tags, for image matching.
Groups local descriptors of one descriptor type within an image template, with flags for binary descriptors and descriptor counts.
Stores an interest point in an image (position, scale, orientation, strength) with an optional local descriptor vector.
A 2x2 float matrix used in vision transformations.
Stores a compressed feature vector at 8 bits per value, decoded by multiplying each byte by a data factor.
Defines a rectangular region of interest in an image by min and max x and y pixel values.

Stores the URL, referer and porn flag for an image plus SafeSearch signals: offensive, violence and spoof scores, face count, OCR annotation, referrer counts and Navboost-based query stats. Sits in the image SafeSearch classification pipeline.
why: Image SafeSearch classification data, narrow to adult content.

summary: Structured postal address (street, locality, administrative area, postal code, country, firm name, language) modelled on the xAL format.
Holds a list of restricts computed before a Mustang index is built.
why: Index-building helper with no described signal.

summary: Per-document data for premium (paywalled) documents in the index: price, currency, publication date, publication fingerprint and entitlement flags.
Proto2's version of MessageSet, an extension container. It lists no attributes here.
Stores a transcript of a video document's audio track with the speech recognition model, language, document keys and URL, so video content can be matched in search.
why: Video transcript data tied to a narrow video corpus.

summary: Holds the complete time-coded transcription text of a document's audio track with timestamp mappings.
Maps character offsets in a transcript to time offsets with a quantized confidence, used to link found snippets to the nearest video time and thumbnail.
Opaque marker describing policy-relevant properties of data objects stored in Google production systems. The docs list no attributes.
Records information about an app annotated for a query: app name, package name, display name, category, confidence and the source of the match.
why: Assistant app understanding, not web search.

summary: Stores per-source data for an app match, including confidence from Navboost, install counts and allow-list or media-provider details.
Records extra flags when an app source is a TV allow list: pre-release mode and unknown device compatibility.
Stores the media provider key and provider type for content served by an app.
Stores a category label and confidence for an app.
Deprecated structure for a custom reminder notification: text, surface type, buttons and tap action.
Defines a notification button with a label and tap action.
Holds the raw URL payload for a notification tap action.
Holds a list of news provider annotations attached to a span of a query, used by the Assistant for news requests.
Describes a news provider: supported locales, official name, pronunciation hint, provider id and a score for how confident the span is a news provider.
Full representation of an Assistant reminder: title, description, time, recurrence, location, creator and recipient, attachments and archived state.
Marks that a reminder came from a document such as Docs, Sheets or Slides. No attributes are listed.
Marks that a reminder came from a Google Chat space. No attributes are listed.
Describes a reminder-triggering location: custom place, chain, category or personal alias, with address, coordinates and feature id.
Stores the category name and display string when a reminder location is a category such as Grocery Stores.
Stores the chain entity id, chain name and feature id when a reminder location is a business chain.
Describes a person other than the user who created or will receive a reminder: name, email, gaia id and photo URL.
Stores the recurrence rule and ids for a repeating reminder.
Stores ringtone sound URLs and the pause between sounds for timer and alarm notifications.
Identifies the room (home graph id and name) in which an alarm or timer sits.
Represents an Assistant timer: creation and expiry times, durations, label, status, device, ringtone and room.

Stores a versioned set of topic embeddings copied from docjoins into shards: compressed page and site embeddings, a site focus score (how focused a site is on one topic) and a site radius (how far page embeddings sit from the site embedding).
why: Documents siteFocusScore and siteRadius topical authority fields.

summary: Holds a list of Android application ids found in a page's outlinks.
why: Apps universal feature, not a web signal.

summary: Holds the data needed to serve one live operation or live event for an app: event id and type, schedule per country, format per locale and priority.
Stores the UTC start, end and optional preview timestamps for one live-op event.
Stores display details for a live-op event: title, description, deeplink and image or video URLs.
Lists all live ops or live events eligible to show for an app package.
Stores an image URL with its height and width.
Groups an app's enhanced cover image, feature graphic and screenshots.

Site-level data for the Firefly ranking change: daily clicks and good clicks, impressions in a boosted period, article counts by 30-day periods, URL counts, first-seen and byline dates, and gambling page counts.
why: Documented site-level click, freshness and article-volume signal.

summary: Records external ids for a local result: Knowledge Graph mid, OpenTable restaurant id and supported Assistant actions.
Holds the list of local intents available for a result in the Assistant dialog.
Generic Assistant representation of a local result: name, address parts, business type, distance, chain flag and external ids.
why: Assistant local result, not web document data.

summary: Defines the client type of a reminder, used for UX customization, metrics, indexing and visibility control.

Stores per-document markup restrictions on previews for EU copyright compliance: maximum snippet length, thumbnail size and video preview seconds, with publisher-set values and sources, plus byline date, first-seen date, AMP flag and favicon display.
why: Snippet and preview limits plus dates tied to web documents.

summary: Records whether a domain is covered by Extended News Previews, with status, desnippeted country codes, policy criteria and version.
why: Domain-level snippet policy for news publishers.

summary: Per-document data for fringe-query ranking: encoded fringe prior scores for the doc, site and entities, XLQ predictions (hoax, translated, YMYL), proximity to fringe-vulnerable seeds, document fringe vulnerability and sensitive entity ids.
why: Documented per-page quality scores for fringe and YMYL handling.

summary: Holds a rewritten query produced by a complex-query system: rewrite type, text and entities.
Stores an entity mid and name referenced by a complex-query rewrite.
Compressed location annotation attached to a document for indexing: top cities, counties, states and countries with their scores, stored as model vocabulary ids.
Holds a list of labels attached to a document or item.
why: Generic label container, signal meaning not described.

summary: Stores one label with id, name, a global value or bucket, and the providers that produced it.
why: Label record; docs do not say what is labelled.

summary: Identifies the provider behind a label (legacy classifiers, a feed or a classifier set id) with a value and bucket.
Click and impression counts used by CRAPS: clicks, good clicks, bad clicks, last-longest clicks, impressions, Unicorn-user clicks and squashed versus unsquashed variants.
why: Documents click, good click and last-longest click counts.

summary: Navboost CRAPS record for a query and URL (or URL pattern) with clicks, good and bad clicks, last-longest clicks and impressions, sliced by country, language, device and location, plus voter token counts and an IP-based prior.
why: Documents Navboost click data per query and URL.

summary: Records the device slice for CRAPS click data: operating system, UX interface (desktop, mobile, tablet) and browser tier.
why: Device slice labels for click data, no signal itself.

summary: Holds CRAPS click signals for one feature slice (country, device, language or location id) plus a voter token bitmap for privacy filtering.
why: Documents click signals sliced by locale and device.

summary: Statistics summary (mean, median, percentiles, variance, weighted count) of per-URL values contributing to pattern-level CRAPS data.
256-bit bitmap used to count distinct voter tokens when merging Glue data, with a single-token shortcut.
Container for versioned experimental NSR-team signals populated at query time for live experiments, not for launches.
why: Experimental NSR signal holder, not a launched signal.

summary: Stores one versioned experimental scoring value, as a bool, number, int or string, with a version id.
Wrapper pairing experimental NSR-team data with the lookup key used to find it in the sitechunk-level WSJ corpus.
why: Experimental NSR data wrapper with a site lookup key.

summary: Stores a versioned site-level Keto score and the fraction of the site used to compute it, propagated into NSR data.
why: Documented site-level quality score with version.

summary: Stores a versioned NSR score value with a version id, used to experiment with the next release.
why: Documents versioned NSR site quality values.

summary: Holds the primary NSR sitechunk (usually the host-level chunk of the canonical URL) and optional secondary, more granular chunks.
why: Defines the site grouping NSR is computed on.

summary: Pairs NSR sitechunks with the source annotator that produced them.

Site-level NSR data: nsr and variance, Chard and Tofu content scores, clutter, article, shopping, UGC, video and YMYL news scores, Keto, SpamBrain LAVC, titlematch, small personal site score, link in and out, impressions, Chrome views, embeddings and cluster ids.
why: Hand-corrected: removed a PageRank mention the module does not document.

summary: Stores uplift-per-cluster values for local sites and small sites used by the Tundra experiment arm.
why: Documents local and small-site uplift in an experiment.

summary: Holds a versioned site2vec embedding as a list of numbers.
why: Site embedding stored in NSR data.

summary: Holds a compressed, versioned site2vec embedding for use in the superroot.
why: Compressed site embedding in NSR data.

summary: Metadata about how NsrData was populated: lookup keys and fields per system (Raffia, Goldmine), processing times and sitechunks used. It is only present in docjoins and MDU shards.
why: Provenance and bookkeeping metadata for NSR data.

summary: Page-level quality data used alongside NSR: URL-level Chard, Tofu, Keto, Rhubarb and VLQ scores, content effort (LLM-based estimate for articles), link incoming and outgoing deltas, offdomain anchor count, autopilot score, predicted default NSR and subchunk adjustment.
why: Documents page-level quality, content effort and link signals.

summary: Records the subchunks looked up for a page's delta adjustment, each with a type (such as ymyl_health), confidence, delta NSR and page weight.
A float value paired with a version id, used across NSR data.
An integer value paired with a version id, used across NSR data.

Stores per-document intent scores (0-100, as parallel lists of intents and scores) for the Orbit Asteroid Belt classifier, plus below-threshold intents and per-image scores. Version field is deprecated.
why: Document-level intent classification stored with the page.

summary: Stores intent scores for images evaluated in the context of a landing page. The docs call this path discouraged in favor of image-only intents.
Stores one image-only Orbit intent: the intent name, its score, whether it triggered at the default threshold, and a flag to remove it when backfilling classifier versions.
why: Image-only intent record, no page-level signal.

summary: Holds the list of image-only Orbit intents with non-trivial scores for an image, plus the classifier version.
Records the snippet chosen for display: rendered HTML, snippet and leading-text type, source decided in PORC, tidbits used, vulgarity flag and trailing ellipsis.
why: Describes the snippet Google picked for a result.

summary: Identifies a single tidbit inside a chosen snippet by section name, token range, separator and text for validation.
why: Locates snippet pieces within page sections.

summary: Holds a snippet candidate with its signal scores, used both for snippet scoring and for Ranklab feature recording. Groups brain, document, quality, query, query-term-coverage and Radish features plus a final score.

Holds data for one title candidate used to score and select SERP titles and to train title models. Includes Goldmine scores and factors (anchor, heading, title tag, Navboost, URL match, trust, site name), source type flags, query match fraction and truncation info.
why: Title candidate scoring features for SERP titles.

summary: Stores the SnippetBrain model score for a snippet candidate and whether SnippetBrain bolding was triggered.
why: Snippet model score and bolding flag.

summary: Undocumented. Per-snippet document-related scores used in snippet scoring, such as salient terms, meta boost, salient position boost, schema.org description boost, leading-text distance and unstable tokens (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Experimental snippet features such as likely-homepage flag and counts of query items, tidbits and visible tokens, plus Radish features (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Quality-related snippet scores such as foreign meta, hidden ratio, redundancy, outlinks, sentence start and token counts (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Query-related snippet scores including query score, Radish score and passage-embedding score (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Coverage values for query terms in the snippet, the title, and title plus snippet (inferred from field names).
why: Query term coverage in title and snippet.

summary: Stores Radish passage signals for a snippet candidate: the Navboost query, passage answer score, passage and snippet coverage, similarity score to the incoming query and passage type.
Stores per-locale product-site data as signals data in docjoins.
why: Product-site data attached to documents per locale.

summary: Stores for one locale a site boosting multiplier and whether the site is a gobi site, a domain boosted for a category query.
why: Per-locale site boost factor for product sites.

summary: Holds a CSE id. The docs say the other fields were defined in 2007 and never used.
why: Legacy custom search engine id, effectively unused.

summary: Annotates which Google or third-party account cross-account personal data came from, for Assistant query rewriting.
Identifies the Google account (email, Gaia id, Dasher and secondary flags) that annotated personal data belongs to.
why: Assistant account provenance, not web search.

summary: Identifies the third-party account (email and provider id) that annotated personal data belongs to.
why: Assistant account provenance, not web search.

summary: Stores alternative contact names with the source they came from and a contact match signal, for Assistant queries.
Undocumented. References a calendar by alias, contact name, family alias or primary alias (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Wraps a contact (person) used as a calendar name (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Holds a family calendar id (inferred from field names).
Stores contact metadata for Assistant queries: names, ids, match types, relationship concepts, account provenance and logging data.
Undocumented. An empty message with no documented fields; likely marks the primary calendar alias (inferred from name).
Wrapper for calendar aliases used in query annotation, defined by extensions because aliases may come from a non-primary account. No fields are listed in the docs.
Stores relationship-to-contact data from Assistant Memory: a contact pointer and the contact name value.
Mustang attachment storing a quantized RankEmbed document embedding in several fixed-point encodings, plus version and improv-query info. Docs say to decode it only through the helper library.
why: Compressed RankEmbed document embedding in Mustang.

summary: Stores a compressed embedding as packed fixed64 values, chosen to save about 14 percent of storage.
Undocumented. Holds a list of launchable-app records for a document (inferred from field names).
why: App link data stored per document.

summary: Stores a compact subset of launchable-app data in PerDocData (Mustang index) so SuperRoot can identify documents containing app links at serving time.
why: Per-document app link data in the index.

summary: Stores a country (2-letter) and how salient it is for the document, on a 0 to 1 scale.
why: Country salience attached to a document.

summary: Stores the set of salient countries for a document, including a packed form optimized for index storage.
Stores set-level data complementing a salient-term set: confidence, head volume ratio, language, virtual volume and per-signal data (body, anchors, clicks).
why: Salient term set stats for a document.

summary: Stores one salient term (unigram or bigram) with salience, weight, original forms and signal-specific data. Under a set it is a normalized term and weight pair.
why: Salient terms describing what a document is about.

summary: Stores a collection of salient terms with weights that describe a document, with set-level data and the version used. Version is specific to web documents.
why: Set of terms Google treats as descriptors of a page.

summary: Stores per-signal (body, anchors, clicks and so on) information for a salient-term set: confidence, volume, bias and noise correction. Most fields exist only in debug mode.
Stores per-signal term-level data behind salient terms, such as centrality, term frequencies, IDF and bigram quality scores. Most fields exist only in debug mode.
Undocumented. Holds a list of Sherlock Knex annotation items (inferred from field names).
why: Entity annotation container, no documented purpose.

summary: Stores one Sherlock Knex annotation: an equivalent mid, a score and calibrated score in 0 to 1, a debug name and a version.
why: Entity annotation with scores, purpose unclear.

summary: Lightweight shopping annotation attached to documents in Muppet, used to score organic shopping results and previews. Stores page-type scores (article, buying guide, forum, Q&A, product review, single or multi product, sold out), shopping-site scores and products. Marked deprecated in favor of UDR.
why: Shopping page-type scores attached to documents; deprecated.

summary: Stores language id and region id as integers for fast scoring in the shopping attachment.
Undocumented. Holds a Moka product-attribute facet id, tag id and measure value (inferred from field names).
Stores offer data matched to an indexed URL: condition, GTINs, image ids, merchant ids, matching type, organic risk score and availability info.
why: Merchant offer data tied to indexed URLs.

summary: Stores product info extracted from product blocks on a page: titles, price and currency, min and max price, free delivery and return flags, and image info.
why: Product data extracted from page blocks.

summary: Undocumented. Holds image height and width (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Holds product data for a shopping attachment: rating, brand entity, catalog and cluster ids, images, offer, product block, relevance embedding (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Holds sitelink candidates generated from breadcrumbs (inferred from the doc: sitelink candidates from breadcrumbs).
Stores a sitelink candidate from breadcrumbs: URL, title, and how many web pages contain that URL in their breadcrumbs.
why: Breadcrumb-derived sitelink candidate with page counts.

summary: Undocumented. Holds sitelink candidate documents with a language, apparently derived from co-clicks (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Holds a candidate URL and title with co-click counts per locale (inferred from field names).
Undocumented. Holds co-click counts (raw, capped, parent) per locale (inferred from field names).

Undocumented fields; the doc says these are scoring signals for computing a sitelink score, mainly for debugging. Field names include long clicks, long CTR, Navboost score, PageRank, Chrome transition counts, impressions, title and navmenu scores.
why: Sitelink scoring inputs incl. clicks, Navboost, PageRank.

summary: Stores scores for normal one-line sitelinks, scroll-to sitelinks and table-of-contents sitelinks. Populated only at serving time.
why: Sitelink-type scores computed at serving time.

summary: Undocumented. Holds a sub-result docid and item metadata (inferred from field names).
Container holding a list of sub-results.
Stores one sitelink target: URL, title, score, languages, mobile flags, scoring signals, snippet response, section texts for page-anchor previews and serving-time signals.
why: A single sitelink target and its scoring data.

summary: Stores a set of sitelink targets with a label, country and language, plus breadcrumb, co-click and two-level targets, top URLs and scoring signals.
why: Group of sitelink targets for a page.

summary: Holds metadata about a list item passed from indexing to Muppet. Its one field is deprecated and no longer populated.
Undocumented. Holds a URL and a score (inferred from field names). A parent field says top URLs are ranked by two-level score, i.e. Chrome transition clicks.
why: Top URL entry with a score.

summary: Undocumented. Holds a first-level sitelink target and its second-level targets (inferred from field names).
Records a bolded range in printed snippet lines: begin and end positions, type and debug text.
why: Which parts of a snippet are bolded.

summary: Stores a byte offset and index marking a position in a bolded snippet range.
Stores per-URL unreliable-dates signals: per-category scores, a max unreliable-dates score and an exposure-adjusted version. Missing scores mean the date is treated as reliable.
why: Records how unreliable a page's dates are.

summary: Stores the LastSignificantUpdate date for a page (Unix seconds), its source, adjustment info and date unreliability info.
why: Last significant update date for a page.

summary: Stores debug info on how a LastSignificantUpdate was adjusted, including the passage-timestamp upper bound and the dropped unbounded timestamp.
why: Adjustments to the last significant update date.

summary: Stores flags for whether a page is classified as a forum page, a Q&A page, or has a fresh repeated date sequence.
why: Page-type flags used in date handling.

summary: Stores unreliable-date signals per domain and Petacat vertical: content-age reliability, date exposure, date-vs-contentage skew, forum/Q&A/social probability and a final unreliable-dates score.
why: Per domain and vertical date reliability scores.

summary: Stores a date extracted from page text: epoch date, byline date, date range, position, precision mark and flags for use in date restricts, ranking trust and snippet byline display.
why: Extracted page date and how it is used.

summary: Stores a start and end for a date range used when a single date plus precision mark is not good enough.
why: Date range extracted from a page.

summary: Stores begin and end byte offsets of a date in the document body so snippet code can locate a byline date.
why: Location of the byline date in page text.

summary: Stores signals data in docjoins for good travel sites: site, type, total quality score, raw signals, entity/aggregator/official flags and a local anchor normalization factor.
why: Travel site quality score and type.

summary: Undocumented. Holds a locale and a type (inferred from field names).
why: Per-locale type for good travel sites.

summary: Stores a named raw signal and its value that determine the travel site quality score.
why: Raw inputs to travel site quality score.

summary: Stores audio-based language of a Watch Page, as detected by Automatic Language Identification, plus the type of detected speech.
Stores cluster scoring info for an entity: cluster id, cluster set confidence, sibling mids, entity score within the cluster and sub-clusters.
Undocumented. Wraps annotations run over auto-generated video captions (inferred from field names).
Stores annotations for a video transcript: ASR repair results, language, punctuated transcript, SAFT sentence data, timing info, transcript source and Webref entities.
why: Video transcript annotations for video answers.

summary: Stores YouTube caption timing for video answers: duration, uploader name and per-sentence instances.
why: YouTube caption timing for video answers.

summary: Stores HTML byte offsets for a sentence and the matching video start and end times in milliseconds.
Stores domain registration info for a document: the days since January 1 1995 that the domain was last created and last expired.
why: Domain creation and expiry dates per document.

summary: Represents an embedding vector with optional cluster info, compressed value and dense feature values.
Represents a cluster of the embedding space: its id and the squared distance of the embedding to the cluster center.
Holds a list of embedding clusters.
Stores one geographic topic of a document: location name, address, coordinates, Oyster feature id and type, normalized score, confidence and component scores.
why: Geographic location a page is about.

summary: Stores a document's GeoTopics ordered by normalized score, highest first.
Undocumented. Holds a raw score and a type for geo-topicality (inferred from field names; the parent calls these raw scores behind the normalized score).
Stores sentiment snippet info in Mustang: token offsets, phrase type, snippet score and text. Polarity and magnitude fields are deprecated in favor of snippet score.
why: Sentiment snippet annotations stored in the index.

summary: Stores the breadcrumb trail extracted from a document, as a list of crumbs plus the source URL.
why: Breadcrumb trail extracted from a page.

summary: Stores one breadcrumb link: the displayed text and the URL it links to.
Stores app information for rich snippets: name, vendor, category, price, ratings, downloads, screenshots, supported platforms, rank data and trusted genome tags.
why: App rich snippet data extracted from pages.

summary: Stores the top-level Play Store app type (game or application).
why: App type helper for rich snippets.

summary: Stores an app price for a country with ISO currency code.
Stores the chosen language and the Trusted Genome tags matching the document locale for an app.
Undocumented. Holds an app store link, category and chart type with a rank (inferred from field names).
Stores app rank entries and the Playwright category ids used to decide which category to show in app ranking info.
Stores the aggregated score of entities for a given name, aggregated over all sources.
why: Entity-name score aggregation used in entity annotation.

summary: Identifies a set of anchors in the CompositeDoc that WebRef collapsed into one, since they contain the same mentions at the same offsets.
why: Points to collapsed anchors in a document.

summary: Stores a category annotation on a name: the collection hrid and the mid of the category entity.
Stores a debug description of concept annotations. The docs say it is for debugging only and may be absent.
Undocumented. Holds human ratings of WebRef annotations, currently document-level relevance ratings (inferred from the doc).
Stores annotation statistics per token type: average open-world score and counts of ranges with candidates, split by capitalized and uncapitalized.
Stores annotator checkpoint fingerprints with labels, used to track down diffs and non-determinism.
Collects annotator performance data: counts of tokens, mentions, entities and candidate mentions, plus processor timings.
Stores book edition metadata for a book entity: the edition mid and its ISBN.
Undocumented. Holds a score ratio, apparently from a previous bootstrapped model iteration (inferred from field name).
Stores high-level category annotations for documents and queries: category mid, title, HitCat page-classifier confidences, shopping qprime flag and an experimental Discover topic score.
why: Page category annotations with classifier confidence.

summary: Undocumented. Holds a confidence for an experimental browsy topic; the doc says it is experimental and relates to Discover (inferred).
Stores HitCat page-classifier scores for a category: confidence, calibrated cumulative confidence and an experimental confidence. HitCat is the page classifier.
why: HitCat page classifier confidence per category.

summary: Stores whether the QPrime query classifier asserts a category as shopping.
why: Shopping flag from a query classifier.

summary: Stores all category type info for an entity: Freebase types, KG collections, Oyster type, salient verticals4 categories and Wikipedia categories.
Stores metadata about entity clusters: whether an entity is a synthetic set entity and the rule instance that explains the cluster.
Defines a cluster from a list of mids by creating one set that is parent of each listed entity.
An instance of a mid-list cluster rule: the role and the rule itself. Each such rule defines one cluster.
Defines clusters based on a relation (link type): entities linking to the same target through that relation become children of one set.
An instance of a relation cluster rule: the role, the rule and the target entity the links point to.
Describes how a cluster rule was instantiated with a role and concrete arguments, via mid-list or relation rule instances.
why: Explains where an entity cluster came from.

summary: Stores a flattened version of possibly nested knowledge-graph property values, collapsing predicate mids into one list.
Undocumented. Holds a compact knowledge-graph property value with mid, hrid, values and status; the doc says it is analogous to freebase PropertyValue.
Stores a compact knowledge-graph topic as a mid and its property values; analogous to a Freebase Topic.
Stores a single typed knowledge-graph value (bool, int, float, text, URI, datetime, id, enum, proto or compound). The docs note quality and performance issues with this representation.
References a component of a compound mention from an argument value: component index, optional debug entity and function-call name.
why: Internal reference inside entity mention structures.

summary: Stores a bitfield of name types in concept tables; in annotator output only URL and phone number types are populated.

Stores detailed scores for how an entity relates to a document: topicality-related normalized score, doc score, connectedness, relevance score, and flags for author, publisher and reference page, plus author profile URL.
why: Entity topicality and author/publisher flags on a page.

summary: Stores how much support a mention received from results in PostRef. Populated only on request.
Stores per-language display names for an entity, for use in displaying the entity.
Stores per-language display names for an entity (canonical and subject names). The docs mark this data deprecated; live names should come from TopicServer.
Stores per-document relevance ratings for Precision at 5 evaluations done with human raters.

Stores document info copied from the docjoin for WebRef: crawl time, docid, language, URL, title, forwarding URLs, disambiguation-page flag, weighted incoming anchor count, total clicks from Navboost and salient terms.
why: Document metadata copied into entity annotation, incl. anchors and clicks.

summary: Holds domain-specific entity data (for example a Freebase topic, Wikipedia join or Geostore feature) in a message set.
Stores enricher debug data shown only in the WebRef demo: non-mid properties, reference pages and related pages. Not for production use.
why: Debug data for the entity enricher.

summary: Stores all annotations for one entity in a document or query: confidence, topicality score and rank, detailed entity scores, implicit flag, segment mentions and image mentions.
why: Entity topicality and mentions on a page.

summary: Stores a human-readable title, description, language and URL for an entity. The docs say despite the name it affects production because the text feeds ML models.
why: Entity description text used for debugging and models.

summary: Represents all information held for a given entity: id, names, links, reference pages, extra metadata, representations and debug and rating data.
Stores metadata about the nature of a link between entities: aggregate kind flags and per-kind info.
Stores link data for one source: KG property, a co-occurrence score and source type.
why: Entity link source and co-occurrence score.

summary: Stores human ratings collected for an entity name, with language, tags and rating records.
Stores one rater's label, source and comment for an entity name.
Stores a score for an entity under a name: absolute score, score ratio, confidence, volume-based score from sources such as Navboost clicks and anchors, plus pruning and cluster flags.
why: Entity-to-name scoring built from clicks and anchors.

summary: Stores the data for one source of entity names, including all entity scores and the source type.
Stores scores about an entity: entity IDF, alpha IDF for debugging, common n-gram probability and a deprecated name capitalization probability.
Stores ranges of a query explained by an entity or entities it implies, used in partial query interpretation.
why: Query ranges explained by an entity.

summary: Stores a range of the annotated document explained by an entity, as a segment mention.
Stores a region-specific score ratio per entity for a domain and region.

Stores additional entity metadata derived from raw data or other sources: category info, cluster metadata, display info, scores, geo and product metadata, latent entities and special entity type. The docs say it often holds important information.
Stores a verticals4 category id and its relative weight within a distribution.
Holds URLs that forward to a document, used for URL-to-topical-entity entries.
why: Forwarding URL list in document metadata.

summary: Stores a language and namespace type used as modifiers when fingerprinting.
Stores Freebase type info: type name or fingerprint, optional score and provenance.
Identifies a segment index for WebRef segment types not covered by other index messages.
Stores geo-specific entity metadata: address, address synonyms, bounds, area, country code, location, Oyster id, name and timezone.
Stores address-component terms usable as address synonyms: name, language and geocoded type.
Groups link info for all locales: target mid, debug title, boosted-primary-weight flag and per-locale link info.
Groups name info for all variants of a normalized name, with per-variant scores and sources.
Undocumented. Holds human ratings, currently annotation ratings (inferred from field names).
Stores an image-level entity mention with confidence score and image docid. Part of an experimental multiref output.
why: Experimental image mention of an entity.

summary: Identifies image Navboost queries in the CompositeDoc by image docid, image index and query index. The docs warn indices can shift between runs.
why: Index pointers to image Navboost queries.

summary: Identifies the source of Spore segments in the CompositeDoc using nested indices and a type.
Stores the equivalent knowledge-card attribute id for an entity, used for Q&A triggering.
Identifies a knowledge-graph collection by id and a preferred human-friendly debug id.
Holds entities that are latent given an entity, such as a team for a player.
why: Latent entity list for an entity.

summary: Stores a latent entity mid, the sources of the relationship and relatedness scores.
Lightweight serving structure exposing lexical information from WordGraph and LWT annotations downstream, as a list of lexical ranges.
why: Lexical annotation passed downstream from RefX.

summary: Stores a recognized lexicon on a byte range of the query: category, direction, facet mid and begin and end offsets.
Stores a matched lightweight token pattern (such as a locative suffix) with offsets, pattern id and source entity index, passed to downstream clients.
why: Language affix match for entity retrieval.

summary: Undocumented. Collects matched lightweight token patterns for each candidate mention or mention.
Undocumented. Collects matched lightweight token patterns for each name-to-concept entry.
Stores what Google's Webref entity system knows about one localized link between entities: an aggregated score, per-source scores, metadata, and whether this is the preferred direction to keep.
why: Entity-to-entity link bookkeeping, not tied to a web page.

summary: Undocumented. A set of flags describing a link kind between entities, with fields named cluster, geoContainment, implication, latentEntity, mdvc and property (inferred from field names).
Records the type of a linked entity, including the flags for the link kind and the knowledge-graph property name it was extracted from.
A shared string type in Webref that holds a name or text with its language, region, normalized form, source domain and the querybase pipeline it came from.

Stores metadata about MDVC concepts for an entity: dimension and generalization concept ids, whether the topic was synthetically created, and per-vertical data. Several fields are marked as migrating to the per-vertical message.
why: Entity concept metadata, no page signal.

summary: Stores per-vertical MDVC data for an entity: compatible, dimension, generalization and expanded-output concept ids, core-topic flag and resolution priority for the named vertical.

Describes one mention of an entity in a document or query: byte and token offsets, a confidence score that the range refers to the entity, implicit/explicit status, prior probability and name metadata. Webref can annotate several document segments this way.
why: Entity annotation of document text with confidence scores.

summary: Records extra begin/end ranges (byte and token offsets) for an entity mention whose text is discontinuous.
Points to one component of a compound mention by entity, segment and mention index, and marks whether it is the head component.
Records a compound mention as a set of component mentions plus the entity expression indices (MRF) the compound applies to.
Holds debug information for a mention: the original text in the range, a clean version, a snippet of surrounding page text and optional info strings.
Stores evaluation data for a mention, a weight used in an ATM score and an aggregate 0-to-1 correctness rating. The docs say it is never annotated in production.
Stores per-document human ratings of entity mentions: byte range, mention match values and individual mention ratings.
why: Rater evaluation data for Webref mentions.

summary: Records one rater's judgement of an entity mention, such as whether the range is correct, whether the mention is relevant and the rating source and task data.
Identifies which meta content tag in the document (by index and the tag's name attribute) a mention segment came from.
why: Pointer to a meta tag segment.

summary: Debug data collecting signals from one query used for learning name priors: the query, its weight and per-candidate signals.
Debug data for one query and one candidate entity: the entity mid, optional name, a result-entity score and whether the entity came only from strong result entities.

Holds everything known about a specific localized name in Webref: the name string, name-specific scores, per-source scores, n-gram data and categories annotated on the range. A flag controls whether it is included in model creation.
why: Entity name data, no page signal.

summary: Stores name-specific scores that are independent of any entity: total score, idf score, an estimate of open-world volume, context weight and a context fringe score.
Records an n-gram context seen on a document: its text, a weight based on how often it appears, and the entity mentions annotated on it.
why: Entity mentions found in document n-gram contexts.

summary: Records an entity mention matched inside an n-gram context: the entity mid and the average score across occurrences.
why: Small helper for n-gram entity matches.

summary: Stores the Oyster feature type for an entity, a rough category taken from a geostore feature type enum.
Stores one rater's per-document relevance rating for an entity topic, including content relevance, whether the page is about a chain and links to the rating task.
Aggregates human ratings by URL or document fingerprint: entity name ratings, mention ratings and task-level relevance ratings.
Stores one key-value pair for a personalization type with a score for the biasing strength applied (positive for boost, negative for the opposite).
why: Personalized query understanding, not web documents.

summary: Documents details of personalization and contextual scoring decisions from Personalized Query Understanding, as a list of per-type output scores. Visibility is restricted.

Records many boolean facts about an entity name, such as generated, compound, dictionary term, ISBN, phone number, strong identifier or trusted all-caps, plus original name versions. Used in the names pipeline.
Stores source-independent scores for a name variant: an unnormalized prior score that the name refers to the entity and a volume-based part of it.
Holds the scores for a name variant and the source that provided them, in Webref's names preprocessing.
Stores the original (pre-normalization) versions of a name and the total count of such versions across sources.
Records one original name version with its text, the sources it came from, a count and a quality score (more authoritative or more sources scores better).
Documents why a particular document was selected for an entity join, as a list of the sources that suggested the URL.
Records where a suggested URL came from: the original URL and the source name.
Stores one named processor counter and its integer value from Webref annotator runs.
Records nested processor timings from Webref annotation: CPU instructions, wall time, counters and child timings.
Stores shopping-related metadata for an entity in Qref output: product line ids, shopping ids and variant cluster ids.
why: Shopping product metadata, not web search signals.

summary: Identifies a set of NavBoost queries in the CompositeDoc that Webref collapsed into one, by query index and feature indices. The collapsed queries contain the same mentions at the same offsets.
why: Points to NavBoost query data used for annotation.

summary: Holds non-entity annotations of text ranges as a list of segment mentions plus the type of range.
Stores the start offset and token count of an annotated range within a segment.
Encapsulates the textual mention spans extracted from a document, split per token, for Refcon.
Describes a mention Webref annotated in a document as fingerprinted tokens (32-bit short and full), with a deprecated segment type list.
Contains a high-level query statistic for a document: the total query count from all query terms, which the docs say can estimate the document's popularity.
why: Query-count popularity statistic on a document.

summary: Encapsulates additional CompositeDoc metadata needed by Refcon, currently the document's query statistics.
A simplified name representation in Refcon's split concepts table: normalized and original name, languages, idf, prior and flags such as generated, translated or strong identifier.
Stores signals for mining new entity reference pages: a reference page score, book score, single-topicness scores and whether the entity was selected as the reference page owner.
why: Scores which page is the reference page for an entity.

summary: Holds a single Webref mention together with the document segment type it occurs in.
why: Wrapper pairing a mention with a segment.

summary: Holds all entity mentions for one segment of a document (document segments such as content, title and anchors), with the segment type. For queries there is one content segment.

Stores a date range for an entity (for example a person's lifespan or a movie's release date), with start and end dates, the knowledge-graph properties they came from and a confidence that the range is relevant to a document.
why: Entity date ranges tied to document relevance.

summary: A compact form of anchor data from the CompositeDoc: anchor text with counts, aggregated scores, normalized scores and total volume, split into onsite and offdomain anchors. Also tracks anchors pointing to fragments or redirects.
why: Documents anchor text counts and scores, onsite vs offdomain.

summary: Holds a list of simplified anchor entries.
